For the creatively obsessed.

You know that feeling when you've got a great idea and just need to make it happen? No endless planning, no overthinking. Just good creative instincts, a few clever tools and the skills to pull it off.

That’s the energy we’re after.

We're looking for a Content Creator who genuinely loves making things. Someone with great taste, a head full of ideas and the skills to bring them to life. Someone who's just as comfortable behind the camera as they are in front of it, and has the personality to make people want to watch.

And you'll be creating content for people just like you.

A little about us.

Envato is an all-in-one creative toolkit bringing together world-class creative assets, purpose-built AI tools to help people make their ideas real.

Our community is made up of designers, filmmakers, editors and creators who care about craft, love experimenting and are always looking for the next tool, technique or spark of inspiration to make better work.

What's the gig?

You’ll be one of the faces of Envato, creating content that brings our products to life and makes creatives want to try them for themselves.

Think clever product demos, creative experiments, social first videos and tutorials that don’t feel like tutorials. The kind of work that makes someone think, “I need that in my toolkit.”

You’ll own the process from first idea to final edit. Concepting, writing, filming, presenting, editing and experimenting with the latest creative tools, including AI.

One day, you might be bringing a new feature to life. The next, testing a creative technique or finding an unexpected way to tell a story.

This isn’t a content churn role. We want someone who cares about making genuinely good work. Content that entertains, inspires and helps creative people make something better.

Sound like you?

You’re creatively curious and know how to make things people actually want to watch.

You have strong video production and editing skills, a sharp eye for visual craft and a natural presence on camera. You know your way around tools like Premiere Pro, After Effects and Photoshop, and AI is already a meaningful part of how you create. You’re confident using it, excited by what’s possible and thoughtful about how it can make creative work better.

You understand social, but you’re not here to simply copy trends. You know how to find an interesting angle, tell a good story and make work feel fresh.

Most importantly, you love the craft, bring plenty of personality and don’t take yourself too seriously.

Show us what you've got.

Send us one piece of content you’re proud of that shows your creative taste, personality, what you can make and you on camera.

If you’ve used Envato tools or assets to create it, tell us.

Life at Envato

Great work can happen from anywhere and we believe in giving our people the flexibility to make work and life work for them. We're remote first globally, with the option to apply to work from another location for up to three months a year. You'll also get home office and team connection budgets, learning support and study leave, wellbeing benefits, two days of volunteer leave and generous paid parental leave.

We know great people don't always tick every box, particularly those from neurodiverse and underrepresented backgrounds. We value different perspectives and lived experiences, so if the role excites you, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
About Button

Since 2018, Button has been building reliable technology for government and private-sector clients with the goal of creating a more sustainable future through digital transformation. Our agile, multi-disciplinary team works on truly impactful technology projects – from climate action to major funding programs. We create secure, easy-to-use systems through deliberate consideration and iteration. We are passionate about creating stronger communities through technology and continuing to grow across Canada and beyond.

You will work closely with our operations team and subject matter experts to develop responses to Requests for Proposals (RFPs), bids, government procurements, and private-sector competitive opportunities.

Your work will include:

  • Reviewing solicitation documents and identifying requirements, evaluation criteria, and submission risks.
  • Interviewing subject matter experts to gather technical, operational, and business information.
  • Asking thoughtful questions to uncover information that may not be immediately apparent.
  • Synthesizing complex technical concepts into clear, compelling, and persuasive written responses.
  • Developing proposal content that aligns with evaluation criteria and scoring rubrics.
  • Identifying information gaps and working collaboratively to gather what is needed before writing.
  • Using AI tools appropriately to support research, organization, and drafting while applying strong editorial judgment to ensure accuracy, quality, and confidentiality

While producing written work is the outcome of the job, knowing WHAT to write is key to success. You'll need to ascertain highly specialized and often technical information and ensure it's translated in a way that speaks directly to the assessment criteria.

Direct experience with public-sector procurement processes, government funding programs, and writing against scoring rubrics is considered a strong asset.

You may have experience in:

  • Proposal writing
  • Grant writing
  • Government procurement responses
  • Management consulting
  • Public policy
  • Research
  • Technical communications
  • Academic writing (Master's or PhD research)
  • Strategy or business analysis

You don't need to be a subject matter expert or technical yourself but you do need to be experienced and comfortable working with subject matter experts. The strongest proposal writers are exceptional listeners.

You don't simply record what subject matter experts say, you identify what's missing, ask follow-up questions, and uncover the information needed by the evaluators.

While you will not be expected to provide technical architecture or deeply technical summaries, the nature of our work involves delivering digital and technical solutions to our clients. A familiarity and comfort level with technology and technical conversations is important.

You'll likely be successful if you have proven experience:

  • Working with technical subject matter experts
  • Conducting interviews and extracting information from stakeholders, including technical recruiting
  • Turning incomplete or ambiguous information into well-structured written content
  • Writing against evaluation criteria or scoring rubrics
  • Working in fast-paced environments with competing deadlines

We operate in a fast-paced environment and the work will typically be offered in “chunks” as opportunities arise. A flexible schedule with some daytime availability is preferred to support collaboration with internal stakeholders. While the role is remote, most collaboration will occur during standard business hours (9–5 PST).

That said, proposal work is deadline-driven by nature and there will occasionally be “all hands on deck” moments to get a submission across the finish line. We’re looking for people who are comfortable operating in that kind of collaborative, fast-moving environment and who can deliver high-quality work under pressure.

This is a great opportunity for individuals with experience in proposal writing, grant writing, procurement responses, or related work. We are also open to candidates with strong academic writing experience in STEM-related fields (Master’s thesis, PhD, research writing, etc.) who are looking for flexible, on-call type work and can demonstrate strong communication and synthesis skills.

We recognize that AI tools are increasingly part of modern writing workflows and we do leverage these tools in our process; however, we expect candidates to use sound judgment, critical thinking, and strong editing skills to ensure all work is clear, accurate, thoughtful, and free from generic or low-quality “AI slop.” Candidates must also demonstrate experience in appropriate data handling practices and use of discretion regarding what information can and cannot be entered into public AI/LLM tools in order to maintain compliance with privacy, confidentiality, and data protection requirements.

This is being offered as an on-call-type independent contractor opportunity with an hourly rate range of $35–$50/hour depending on experience, expertise, and the nature of the work being assigned.

Salary: 40-50 per hour

jobs.description:
Growth Marketing Lead (AI-First)

Location: Bangalore-based, remote — working core hours that overlap the US day (our team and customers are US-based)

Engagement: Contract to start, with potential to expand

Reports to: Founder / CEO

About MarcoPolo Learning

MarcoPolo Learning builds award-winning learning experiences for young children. Since 2013, we've reached hundreds of thousands of families and thousands of classrooms across North America, with our Emmy-nominated MarcoPolo World School app and The Polos TV series bringing STEM and global discovery to life for early learners.

We're now an AI-first company. Our newest product, Miss Audrey AI, puts a proactive AI coach and teaching assistant in the hands of early-childhood educators, supporting teachers in the moment with guidance, resources and family engagement. It opens up a new category in early learning, and we're building the growth engine to bring it to every teacher, centre and early-learning organisation that needs it. This is the role that leads it.

Backed by top-tier investors and running lean, we're looking for a senior, hands-on growth leader who wants to build that engine with AI at its core.

The role in one line

Lead MarcoPolo's growth. Define the story that makes educators and early-learning leaders see Miss Audrey AI as essential, build an AI-powered engine to reach them at scale, and turn that interest into sign-ups, paid subscribers and sales conversations.

This is not a general marketing role

This is not a single-channel role. It isn't only SEO, paid social, content calendars or app installs. Miss Audrey AI is creating a new category, so growth here comes from sharp positioning, smart outreach and constant experimentation rather than capturing existing search demand. We're looking for a strategic generalist who can set the direction, do much of the work hands-on, and bring the team along.

You'll work in a fast-moving, AI-first startup where AI is built into how marketing gets done, from research and outreach to creative, testing and reporting. You'll be the person who knows which tools are worth using, puts them to work, and keeps raising the bar on what our growth engine can do.

What you'll own

Positioning and messaging. Shape how we talk to teachers, centre directors and early-learning leaders. Test messaging angles quickly, learn from the results and sharpen the story until it consistently converts.

An AI-powered growth engine. Design and run AI-driven workflows for audience research, prospect enrichment, personalised outreach across email, LinkedIn and other channels, creative, landing pages and reporting. Review the output, refine it and keep improving it.

The Miss Audrey AI funnel. Take educators from free sign-up to first value to paid subscription, working with engineering on onboarding, upgrade moments and lifecycle messaging.

Pipeline for our sales team. Turn campaigns and product usage into qualified conversations with centre directors and organisation leaders, and equip our US sales team with the messaging and evidence to close.

The experiment loop. Decide what to test across audiences, messages, channels and offers; read the results; and double down on what works.

Tools and innovation. Stay ahead of the AI marketing landscape. Evaluate new tools, adopt the ones that move the needle, and help the wider team use them.

Leadership and communication. Present plans and results to leadership, explain the approach clearly to the team, direct freelancers and partners, and help build the function as it grows.

Report the numbers that matter. Pipeline, sign-ups, activation, paid conversion and cost to acquire, with a clear point of view on what to do next.

Expected outcomes

You'll be measured on results, not activity:

  • Messaging: a clear, tested value proposition that resonates with teachers, centre directors and early-learning leaders.
  • Growth engine: a live, AI-powered acquisition and outreach engine producing a steady flow of qualified sign-ups and conversations.
  • Conversion: a measurable and improving free-to-paid conversion rate for Miss Audrey AI.
  • Sales pipeline: a reliable flow of qualified opportunities handed to the US sales team.
  • Experimentation: a regular testing cadence across messaging, channels and offers, with results that compound.
  • Capability: new AI tools and workflows adopted across marketing, and a clear plan for how the function scales.

What you'll need (essential)

  • 7+ years in growth or marketing across strategy, positioning and messaging, demand generation, lifecycle and experimentation. You're a generalist with real breadth, not a single-channel specialist.
  • Leadership experience. You've owned a growth or marketing function, or a major part of one: setting strategy, directing people, agencies or freelancers, and working closely with founders or senior leadership.
  • AI-first in practice. You use AI tools daily in your marketing work and can show workflows you've built and deployed. You keep up with the AI marketing landscape and know which tools are worth using.
  • Experience building demand for a new or differentiated product, where you shaped the story and made the case rather than capturing existing demand.
  • A confident, clear communicator, with excellent spoken and written English. You're comfortable presenting to leadership, working with a US-based team and customers, and explaining strategy simply.
  • Data and experimentation fluency. Comfortable setting up measurement, reading funnel and campaign data, and running clean experiments.
  • Startup pace and self-direction. You ask the right questions, propose a plan and execute with minimal oversight in a fast-changing environment.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience marketing to educators, schools, childcare or early-learning organisations, or to individual users within larger organisations.
  • Freemium or product-led growth experience, converting free users into paying subscribers.
  • Experience working with or for a US-based company while based in India; you understand US customers, US working styles and collaborating across time zones.
  • Prior startup experience: you know what it's like to build with limited resources and moving goalposts.

Nice to have

  • EdTech, or any product sold to educators, parents or consumers.
  • Familiarity with tools already in use here, including HubSpot, Customer.io, n8n, ClickUp and Webflow, and with AI-driven prospecting and outreach tools.
  • Enough design sense to shape clean, conversion-focused web and email flows (you don't need to be a visual designer).

Engagement details

  • Type: Contract to start, with potential to expand as the growth engine proves out.
  • Location & hours: Bangalore-based and remote, with daily working overlap with our US team.
  • Works closely with: The US sales team and AI-automation partners who support the technical build.
  • Start: Immediate start preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.excerpt: This position is fully remote/home based.  Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK.
jobs.description:
This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK.

Role Summary

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively.

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades.

That means there are interesting product problems to solve - not just features to deliver.

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions.

You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it.

How we work

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty.

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions.

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them.

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something.

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are.

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll:

  • Understand the problem. Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them.
  • Shape product direction. Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities.
  • Practise continuous discovery. Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data.
  • Turn uncertainty into learning. Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction.
  • Make good product decisions. Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue.
  • Measure whether things are getting better. Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect.
  • Work iteratively. Help the team deliver in small steps, learn from what happens and adapt rather than treating plans as fixed commitments.
  • Communicate your thinking. Clearly explain problems, evidence, choices, trade-offs and learning to people with very different levels of technical and product knowledge.
  • Create strong feedback loops. Use conversations, demos, reviews and other forums to get useful feedback early rather than presenting finished thinking late.
  • Work as part of a team. Create the conditions in which designers, engineers and other specialists can contribute to product decisions rather than treating product management as something the PM does alone.
  • Look beyond the product interface. Understand the wider service, including processes, systems and teams around it, and recognise when solving a user problem requires changing more than software.

Experience and qualifications

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience. 
  • Using creative problem solving to build software solutions.
  • Demonstrate experience working as a Product Manager in a multidisciplinary digital product team, working closely with disciplines such as design, engineering, research and delivery.
  • Experience using product discovery alongside delivery - for example, user research, data, experimentation and hypothesis testing - to understand problems and inform what a team should do next.
  • Experience working with significant uncertainty or ambiguity: identifying what is known, what is assumed and what needs to be learned before making larger commitments.
  • Experience taking complex problems and helping a team turn them into clear priorities, outcomes and practical next steps.
  • Experience making product decisions using a combination of user evidence, data, organisational goals, technical constraints and product judgement.
  • Experience communicating product thinking clearly to a wide range of people, including explaining evidence, uncertainty, trade-offs and why particular decisions have been made.
  • Experience working collaboratively with people outside the immediate product team, particularly where different groups have different needs, incentives or perspectives.

Particularly useful

We'd be especially interested in candidates who have experience of one or more of the following:

  • Working in an organisation going through significant product, digital or organisational transformation.
  • Working in complex service environments where improving the user experience involves changes to technology, operations, policy or organisational processes - not simply changing an interface.
  • Helping teams move towards more iterative, outcome-focused or evidence-led ways of working.
  • Working in a mission-led, research, publishing, education, scientific or other knowledge-based organisation.

Experience of scholarly publishing is useful but isn't required.

What we're looking for in a Senior Product Manager

For us, seniority isn't about having a larger backlog or knowing more product framework: it's about judgement.

You'll be able to take a complex and uncertain problem, help people understand it, decide what we most need to learn, bring a team together around a sensible course of action and change that course when the evidence tells us to.

You'll be comfortable making decisions without perfect information while being clear about the assumptions and risks involved.

And you'll help the people around you think more clearly about the product - not simply tell them what to build.

Working at PLOS

You'll join PLOS's Product team and work collaboratively with colleagues across Digital and the wider organisation.

The role has no direct line-management responsibility.

The job is fully remote. Some flexibility to work across time zones and occasional national or international travel may be required.

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is (UK) £65,000 - £73,500. PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below.

BENEFITS:

  • Private medical insurance
  • Life assurance
  • Income protection 
  • Personal accident insurance
  • Pension with up to 10% employer match
  • 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out.

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all.

Visit to learn more.

To learn more about how PLOS protects your privacy, see our Employee Privacy Notice.

jobs.excerpt: Reddit is a community of communities.  It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet.
jobs.description:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit .

Reddit is a complex consumer ecosystem where users, content, communities, and conversations interact over time. We are looking for a very senior data science thought leader to shape how Reddit understands and improves that ecosystem for the user / consumer flywheel.

This role will define the measurement, modeling, and experimentation strategy for major Consumer questions: how users discover value, form habits, and deepen engagement; how we understand and serve user intent; how content and communities evolve; and how our systems create durable value for users, contributors, communities, and Reddit.

The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in one or more areas of consumer science, such as:

  • Recommender systems and information retrieval
  • User modeling, personalization, lifecycle, LTV, or optimization
  • Content, community, or ecosystem modeling
  • Knowledge graphs and representations of users, content, and communities
  • Causal inference, experimentation, and long-term consumer measurement

You will partner with leaders across Product, Engineering, Research, and Community to turn ambiguous consumer problems into clear scientific questions, durable analytical systems, and decisions that improve Reddit at scale.

What you’ll do

  • Set the scientific direction for high-impact Consumer problems spanning discovery, relevance, personalization, user growth, retention, content, and communities.
  • Build a durable understanding of users, their intent, their needs, and the behaviors that lead to lasting value
  • Develop models and frameworks that represent users, content, communities, and their relationships over time for use in systems that operate at scale
  • Determine how to measure consumer and ecosystem health when objectives compete and short-term engagement may differ from long-term value.
  • Set learning agendas and steer experimentation strategy to distinguish durable improvement from temporary metric movement.
  • Build state-of-the-art measurement systems to evaluate heterogeneous effects across user personas, acquisition cohorts, platforms, content types, and community stages, and guide their actionability in production environments
  • Ensure coherence around ecosystem interactions including feedback loops, selection effects, interference, distribution shift, content supply, and other ecosystem risks.
  • Translate complex technical findings into clear product and business decisions.
  • Develop exceptional scientists through mentoring and influence data science org health and direction

Requirements

  • Deep expertise in at least one relevant area, with the breadth and curiosity to work across adjacent domains.
  • A deep understanding of how to model and optimize systems involving users, content, communities, and feedback loops.
  • Ability to frame and lead the most ambiguous questions, identify the most important uncertainties, and develop a rigorous path from evidence to action.
  • Exceptional technical judgment across model design, objective selection, validation, experimentation, and production tradeoffs.
  • Advanced knowledge of modern machine-learning methods for behavioral and content data, including representation learning and sequential or contextual models. Experience with deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
  • Experience working across Product, Engineering, Research, and other partner teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and explain technical ideas clearly.
  • Significant experience applying data science, machine learning, statistics, experimentation, or causal inference to complex consumer products.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Program Overview

The World Health Organization projects a global shortfall of 11 million health workers by 2030, increasingly concentrated in the African region. This includes a shortage of nearly 900,000 midwives (Nove et al., 2021) and a similar gap in children's nurses, who make up only around 2% of the nursing workforce in several African countries, despite children comprising up to half the population (North et al., 2019). These shortages are closely linked to preventable maternal, newborn, and child deaths and high under-five mortality. WHO Afro modelling estimates that health workers required a $36.3 billion wage bill in 2022, against an available financing envelope of just $20.85 billion—a 43% workforce financing gap across the region's 47 countries. This constrained fiscal space is prompting governments and partners to rethink traditional workforce approaches, including how new technologies, such as AI-enabled tools for training, clinical decision support, and workflow efficiency, can extend the reach and impact of a limited workforce, while keeping health workers and human connection at the centre of care. In May 2026, African governments adopted the Accra Declaration at the Africa Health Workforce Investment Forum, committing to concrete action on planning, training, and retaining the continent's health workforce.

Against this backdrop, a multi-country health workforce initiative is being set up to strengthen the availability, quality, distribution, and retention of primary health care and maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) workers across the Africa region. The initiative will support government-led efforts to close these gaps — including shortages in nursing, midwifery, MNCH specialists, allied health cadres, and community health workers — that limit access to quality primary MNCH care.

The initiative will be informed by a country-led planning process, partnering with governments, training institutions, and implementing organizations to strengthen health workforce policy, planning, and financing systems; expand and improve training capacity; support the equitable distribution and retention of health workers; and address gaps in medical equipment and facility infrastructure that limit health worker effectiveness and retention.

A secretariat is being set up at CHAI Ghana to provide technical, programmatic, and financial management assistance to participating governments and partners, including workforce planning and training design, monitoring and evaluation, and alignment with the initiative's technical framework and country priorities.

Position Overview

The Evidence, Learning, and Information Systems Director is responsible for tracking the initiative’s progress against its goals and targets, and for coordinating the overall M&E approach across governments, the Secretariat, and academic/evaluation partners.

During inception, they will design an M&E system that tracks progress of the initiative, while also strengthening countries’ national data systems. During planning, they will advise on information system-related interventions at the country level needed to track progress. They will also ensure that all country-level plans include robust M&E plans mapped to initiative-level targets and indicators. During implementation, they will maintain a dashboard tracking progress against indicators and lead the Secretariat in data-driven course correction when necessary. They will also lead the initiative’s research agenda and learning processes, ensuring that insights from data and lessons from programming are disseminated and applied across the initiative as they emerge. During close-out, they will compile all data and prepare final reports. They will supervise one or more M&E officers – exact roles and team structure will be finalized following the co-creation of the M&E approach.

Responsibilities

Inception

  • Design the initiative’s M&E system with a focus on building government data systems at the country level.
  • Develop the core indicator and data reporting template and contribute to the narrative reporting template.

Country planning

  • Advise on information-systems-related interventions needed at country level.
  • Provide technical guidance on system design and indicator development, including via review of country-level plans.

Implementation

  • Oversee a dashboard tracking progress against indicators and lead the initiative in data-driven course correction when necessary.
  • Manage reporting on progress towards the initiative’s goals.
  • Lead the initiative’s learning processes, ensuring insights from data and program lessons are disseminated and applied across the initiative as they emerge.
  • Coordinate a technical advisory group of leaders in health systems research (drawn from academic institutions, multilaterals, and government) providing strategic and methodological guidance to M&E and research.
  • Engage, as required, and manage contracted academic and evaluation partners executing more in-depth analysis, quasi-experimental studies, and peer-reviewed research.
  • Steward the initiative’s research agenda.

Management

  • Supervise one or more M&E Officer(s).

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of public health experience in planning, project/change management, stakeholder coordination, capacity building, and program performance management.
  • Experience designing and implementing a centralized M&E system from the ground up, including frameworks, tools, and guidelines.
  • Familiarity with government health information systems in sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience with M&E capacity building and knowledge management, including training and community-of-practice leadership.
  • Program management experience across health system strengthening initiatives, coordinating with academic research institutions, government ministries, implementing partners, and donors.
  • Experience working as an academic researcher or with academic researchers in the public health field.
  • Advanced degree in a relevant field.
  • In-depth knowledge of health workforce and health systems programming in East, West, and/or Southern Africa.
  • Technical and programmatic experience in health workforce, financing, systems, PHC, and MNCH, including measurement and data use in these areas.
  • Experience working with private philanthropies, engaged boards, and donor reporting.
  • Lived experience, extensive knowledge, and understanding of the cultural, political, and economic context in African countries.
  • Ability to inspire, motivate, and manage a diverse and geographically dispersed team.
  • Willingness to travel regularly internationally.
  • English fluency required.
  • Working French or Portuguese is an advantage.

Job Title: Senior Clinical Research Associate - Spain - Oncology + Hematology - Remote

Job Location: Barcelona, Spain

Job Location Type: Remote

Join a global Contract Resource Organization (CRO) where innovation meets purpose. At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we're driven by a shared commitment to improving lives through high-quality clinical research. Our teams are empowered to think creatively, take ownership, and deliver meaningful work that helps bring life-changing therapies to patients around the world.


With more than 4,000 professionals across the globe, we foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, growth is encouraged, and every contribution makes an impact. Whether you're building your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and help shape the future of clinical research.


Make an Impact as a Senior Clinical Research Associate at Worldwide

As a Senior Clinical Research Associate, you’ll play a key role in protecting patient safety, maintaining high-quality clinical data, and ensuring investigative sites deliver studies in line with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), regulatory requirements, protocols, and SOPs.

You’ll take ownership of the full site monitoring lifecycle, from qualification and initiation through interim monitoring, site management, and close-out. You’ll work closely with sites and study teams to strengthen protocol adherence, resolve data queries, maintain essential documentation, and ensure safety information is appropriately reviewed and reported.

You’ll also have the opportunity to bring your experience beyond individual sites, acting as a Lead CRA on global studies, coordinating and mentoring CRAs, contributing to monitoring plans, reviewing visit reports, delivering training, and supporting study milestones.


Where You'll Work

This is a home-based Clinical Research Associate role supporting sites across Spain. Candidates must reside within the territory to effectively support site visits and study activities. You will collaborate with sites, sponsors, and global study teams while traveling to investigative sites approximately 8-10 days per month.


What You'll Do

  • Lead site qualification, initiation, interim monitoring, management, and close-out activities, ensuring compliance with protocols, GCP, applicable regulations, and SOPs.
  • Protect patient safety and data integrity by reviewing informed consent and safety information, conducting source document verification, reviewing CRFs, and supporting timely query resolution.
  • Guide sites in protocol adherence, Investigator Site File maintenance, regulatory and ethics documentation, investigational product accountability, and ongoing study requirements.
  • Coordinate CRAs as a Lead CRA on global studies and provide mentoring, training, accompanied visits, and practical guidance to less experienced colleagues and site staff.
  • Partner with Project Management and study teams to evaluate deliverables, study milestones, site performance, and monitoring activities.
  • Develop monitoring plans, study-specific tools, templates, and training materials as requested to support consistent study delivery.
  • Review site visit reports and provide clear feedback and edits while ensuring relevant site documentation is maintained for filing in the Trial Master File.
  • Contribute your clinical monitoring expertise to study team and investigator meetings, bid defenses, and the design of protocols and CRFs.

What You'll Bring

  • Education and CRA experience: an MD or Pharmacy qualification (MSPH, PharmD, PhD, equivalent Pharmacy degree, or similar) with at least 3 years’ CRA experience; or a minimum four-year college curriculum in medical, biological, physical, health, pharmacy, or another related science with at least 5 years’ CRA experience; or a two-year college curriculum or equivalent education/training, preferably a nursing or equivalent life science degree, with at least 7 years’ CRA experience.
  • Extensive knowledge of clinical research principles and processes, with a thorough understanding of FDA and/or EU regulations and directives, ICH Guidelines, local regulatory requirements, and SOPs.
  • Strong therapeutic-area expertise, with a thorough understanding of two to three therapeutic areas sufficient to operate as a Lead CRA where appropriate.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, planning, organizational, time-management, initiative, and problem-solving skills, alongside the ability to lead and motivate an assigned team when applicable.
  • Technical proficiency with Microsoft Office, IxRS, and electronic data capture (EDC) systems.
  • Experience in full-service monitoring PREFERRED.
  • Valid current passport and driving licence, with willingness to travel as required.
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English, together with fluency in the local languages of the countries under responsibility.

jobs.title: Senior Information Systems Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era.
jobs.description:
Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role

We are seeking a talented and experienced Sr Information Systems Engineer to join Cribl's IT Engineering team. In this role, you will be the technical owner of the core systems that power how Cribl operates every day — from identity and access to endpoints, cloud infrastructure, and the automations that tie it all together. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role on a team that treats reliability, security, and employee experience as equally important outcomes.

You'll partner closely with Security, Enterprise Applications, and People teams to design and run the services Cribl depends on at scale: Okta, AWS, ServiceNow, MDM, and a growing stack of SaaS integrations and AI-powered workflows. Whether you're building joiner/mover/leaver automations, hardening endpoint baselines, or governing the next generation of MCP-connected AI tools, your work will be foundational to how a fast-moving, remote-first company stays secure and operational.

This role reports to IT Engineering leadership and will serve as a senior peer and escalation point across the IT & Security organization.


As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

As the Sr Information Systems Engineer, you will be the technical owner of Cribl's core corporate systems — keeping identity, endpoints, cloud infrastructure, and IT automation healthy, secure, and scalable. Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Identity, Access & Lifecycle: Own administration of our primary identity provider (Okta or equivalent) and design joiner/mover/leaver automations (e.g., Workday → Okta → SaaS) with a focus on least privilege, auditability, and contractor and elevated-access workflows.
  • AWS, Cloud & Core Infrastructure: Administer AWS accounts used for corporate IT, VPN, and supporting infrastructure, including secure networking patterns, logging, monitoring, and alerting across IT-owned cloud resources.
  • Endpoint Management & MDM: Own endpoint management for macOS and Windows via MDM (e.g., Jamf, Intune), including zero-touch provisioning, patch management, security baselines, and compliance reporting for the fleet.
  • ServiceNow & IT Service Management: Serve as primary ServiceNow administrator for IT & Security — core data model, catalog, workflows, SLAs, and integrations — and partner with Security, Finance, and Compliance to support ITGC, SOX/IT controls, access reviews, and change management.
  • Automation, Integrations & Tooling: Design and maintain automation workflows across IT systems (e.g., Okta Workflows, Serval, Zapier, PowerShell/Python, APIs) and serve as SME for SaaS integrations across Okta, ServiceNow, Google Workspace, Slack, and Azure/AWS.
  • AI Tools & MCP Governance: Evaluate, configure, and govern AI tools and MCP-based agent frameworks in partnership with IT and Security, ensuring safe usage patterns, appropriate access controls, and clear documentation and runbooks.
  • Operations, Support & On-Call: Serve as Tier 3 escalation for complex incidents across identity, MDM, ServiceNow, and core platforms; participate in the IT on-call rotation; and contribute to IT metrics, fleet reporting, and knowledge base content.

We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones - you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.


If You’ve Got It - We Want It

  • Corporate IT Systems Experience: 5+ years in corporate IT roles with significant responsibility for systems administration across identity, SaaS, and/or infrastructure in a cloud-first environment, with a proven track record balancing project work and operational/on-call responsibilities.
  • AWS Administration (Required): Hands-on, production experience with AWS (IAM, VPCs, EC2/ECS or similar, basic networking, tagging/governance) supporting internal IT or SaaS platforms.
  • ServiceNow Administration: Hands-on administration of ServiceNow or a similar enterprise ITSM platform, including workflow configuration, catalog items, change/incident processes, and basic reporting.
  • Enterprise Identity Provider Experience: Direct, production experience with at least one enterprise identity provider — Okta strongly preferred; Azure AD/Entra ID or similar acceptable — including SSO, lifecycle management, and access policies.
  • Endpoint Management Ownership: Demonstrated ownership of macOS and/or Windows endpoint management in a mid-to-large fleet, including baseline configs, software distribution, and patch management.
  • Scripting & Automation: Experience with at least one scripting language (Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar) and comfort working with REST APIs and JSON.
  • Remote-First Operator: Comfortable working autonomously in a fast-moving, distributed environment — you manage your own priorities, communicate proactively, and know when to escalate.
  • Preferred Qualifications
    • Experience with Jamf (macOS), Intune (Windows/mobile), and/or device posture tooling such as Kolide or similar.
    • Experience managing core SaaS tools such as Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Atlassian, or Glean.
    • Background designing or maintaining automations with tools like Serval, Zapier, or equivalent orchestration platforms.
    • Experience evaluating, configuring, and governing AI tools and agents (e.g., Claude, Gemini, Glean) and MCP-based agent frameworks in an enterprise environment.
    • Working knowledge of Azure (subscriptions, RBAC, group-based access) and/or other major cloud providers alongside AWS.
    • Prior experience supporting a rapidly scaling, distributed engineering organization.

The salary for this role is dependent on geographic location and will be based on the individual candidate's job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

In addition to base salary, for sales and some sales-adjacent roles, employees are eligible to earn incentive compensation (commission). For all other roles, employees are eligible to participate in the Cribl Corporate Bonus Program.

In addition to a competitive salary, Cribl also offers a generous benefits package which includes health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and paid time off, a fertility treatment benefit, 401(k), and equity.

Base Salary Range
$99,000—$156,000 USD

Bring Your Whole Self
Diversity drives innovation, enables better decisions to support our customers, and inspires change for the better. We’re building a culture where differences are valued and welcomed, and we work together to bring out the best in each other. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.

Regional Sales Director

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Compliance / Operational Excellence

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of people leadership experience in a district / regional manager role

  • Prior launch experience required; first-launch / startup biotech experience strongly preferred
  • Experience in cardiovascular, nephrology, hypertension, or related specialty markets strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated success in recruiting and developing top talent
  • Strong business planning, analytical, and coaching skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment
  • Willingness to travel extensively within region

Leadership Profile

  • A strong coach who develops people and builds winning teams
  • Highly accountable, with a bias for action and urgency
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and helping build infrastructure
  • Collaborative and able to influence across functions
  • Resilient, adaptable, and energized by launch environments

Travel

  • This position requires up to 60% travel. Frequently travel is outside the local area and overnight.

These positions are eligible for standard Company benefits including medical, dental, vision, time off and 401K, as well as participating in Mineralys incentive plans are contingent on achievement of personal and company performance. jobs.excerpt: DescriptionMEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.
jobs.description:
Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.

We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As Staff Product Designer, you will own the end-to-end design of MEDvidi's AI Track, the core line of AI-powered clinical tools where providers interact with model outputs in a regulated healthcare environment. Your design decisions directly shape how clinicians review, accept, and correct AI-generated notes, treatment plans, and recommendations, impacting both provider efficiency and patient outcomes.

You will work closely with product managers and engineers, reporting to the Director of Product. This is a senior IC role with no direct reports: you drive product design from problem definition through delivery, gather requirements independently, and bring solutions to release. Your scope includes provider-facing tools (Chart Review, AI Scribe, AI Receptionist), patient portal, and internal operational systems, all web-based.

Why this role

  • Zero-to-one in AI-first environment. You will shape new interaction patterns for agentic AI features: Chart Review, AI Scribe, AI Receptionist, where design quality directly affects clinical decisions.
  • Prototype in real code, not Figma mockups. Prototyping happens in Claude Code and Cursor on the actual codebase with production components. Your prototypes go straight to engineering without redrawing.
  • Co-own a design system built for humans and AI agents. You will evolve reusable components, tokens, and documentation that are readable by both your teammates and code-generation agents, a rare opportunity to define what design systems look like in an AI-native workflow.

Responsibilities

  • Own product design in your areas of the AI Track end-to-end: from defining the problem with the product manager, through user analysis, to working with engineers on the solution and accepting the build.
  • Design and iterate on human-AI interaction patterns: interfaces where providers verify, accept, edit, or reject model output and bring those patterns to a state where other teams can reuse them.
  • Ensure quality of design decisions: validate solutions with users when needed, perform design acceptance with engineering, analyze post-release results, and feed learnings back into the product.
  • Contribute to the design system within product initiatives: turn your solutions into reusable components in Storybook with tokens, naming, and documentation that are usable by both designers and AI code-generation agents.
  • Gather requirements independently: go to providers, medical operations, and product managers, identify problems, and bring back a proposal. There is no standing PM brief in AI Track, you shape the brief.
  • Accelerate design delivery using AI tools: build functional prototypes in Claude Code or Cursor on the real codebase with production components; prototypes go to engineering without redrawing.

This role is not for you if

  • You need a detailed brief before starting work. Requirements here are gathered by you, not handed to you, there is no PM or BA writing specs for AI Track.
  • You prefer managing people over hands-on design. This is an IC role with no direct reports; the impact comes from the quality of your own design decisions.
  • You design exclusively in Figma and hand off static specs. Prototyping at MEDvidi happens in code on the real codebase using AI agents, comfort with a code editor is a daily requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Requirements

  • 6+ years in product design, with a focus on complex work interfaces: EHR, admin panels, CRM, operational tools, or other systems where specialists perform their core work.
  • Demonstrable experience designing human-AI interaction: interfaces where users verify, accept, edit, or reject model output. Building a 0-to-1 agentic product is ideal; experience with review-and-approval interfaces for automated decisions also qualifies.
  • Hands-on prototyping in code using AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent) on an existing component library or codebase, not just design tools.
  • Track record of contributing to a design system within product work: shipping reusable components, tokens, and documentation as part of feature delivery, not as a standalone project.
  • Proven ability to gather requirements independently, finding problems, talking to users and stakeholders, and driving a solution to release without waiting for a mandated brief.
  • Advanced English (B2+) and fluent Russian.
  • Availability to work within CET-compatible hours.

Would be a plus

  • Experience in healthcare or telemedicine products: understanding of HIPAA, clinical compliance constraints, and the provider's role in decision-making.
  • Experience leading a design team's transition to AI tools: setting up shared agent workflows, running workshops, driving adoption across peers.
  • Hands-on user research with specialist users: usability testing and interviews with doctors, nurses, or clinical operators (not only end consumers).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.
  • Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation.
  • Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply.
  • Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days.
  • Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events.

Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let's build something meaningful together.

﻿

MEDvidi is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and contractors. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Legal Intern (Unpaid / Academic Credit Eligible)

FASD United – Justice Advisory Committee / Justice Center

Location: Remote (U.S.-based required)

Duration: Semester-based (Fall/Spring/Summer; flexible start dates)
Time Commitment: 10–15 hours per week (flexible based on academic requirements)
Compensation: Unpaid (academic credit or volunteer experience)

Position Overview

FASD United is seeking law students for a Legal Internship supporting its Justice Advisory Committee and Justice Center initiatives. This role offers hands-on experience at the intersection of law, disability, behavioral health, and public policy, with a focus on improving justice system outcomes for individuals with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD).

Interns will contribute to legal research, training development, and the creation of case-informed resources that support attorneys, courts, families, and policymakers.

Key Responsibilities

Legal Research & Analysis

  • Conduct legal research on topics related to FASD and the justice system (e.g., competency, Miranda rights, sentencing, diversion, disability accommodations)
  • Identify and summarize relevant case law, statutes, and emerging legal trends
  • Support development of legal briefs, memoranda, and issue summaries

Amicus Brief Support

  • Assist in research and drafting components of amicus curiae briefs
  • Compile supporting evidence, citations, and interdisciplinary research (legal + clinical)
  • Track relevant appellate and post-conviction cases involving FASD-related issues

Training & Resource Development

  • Support the development of training materials for legal professionals (judges, defense attorneys, prosecutors, law enforcement)
  • Assist in creating fact sheets, legal guides, and presentation materials
  • Translate complex legal and clinical concepts into accessible formats

Committee & Program Support

  • Assist with preparation of Justice Advisory Committee materials (agendas, summaries, research briefs)
  • Support coordination of subject-matter experts and contributors
  • Participate in internal discussions and contribute insights where appropriate

Learning Objectives

Interns will:

  • Gain exposure to disability-informed legal frameworks and justice system reform
  • Develop skills in legal research, policy analysis, and applied advocacy
  • Engage with multidisciplinary professionals across law, behavioral health, and social services
  • Build experience in nonprofit legal strategy and systems-level impact work

Qualifications

  • Current law student (1L, 2L, or 3L) in good academic standing
  • Strong legal research and writing skills
  • Interest in criminal law, juvenile justice, disability law, public defense, prosecution, or public policy
  • Ability to synthesize complex information across disciplines
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail

Preferred (Not Required)

  • Coursework or experience in criminal law, evidence, constitutional law, or disability rights
  • Interest or experience related to FASD, neurodevelopmental disabilities, or behavioral health
  • Experience with legal databases (e.g., Westlaw, LexisNexis)

Supervision & Structure

  • Interns will be supervised by FASD United staff and/or designated legal advisors affiliated with the Justice Advisory Committee
  • Regular check-ins and feedback will be provided
  • Work may contribute to real-world legal resources, training materials, and policy initiatives

Academic Credit / Volunteer Structure

  • This is an unpaid position
  • FASD United will support documentation required for academic credit, externship programs, or pro bono hours
  • Interns are responsible for coordinating with their academic institution for credit approval

How to Apply

Please submit:

  1. Resume or CV
  2. Brief statement of interest included in a cover letter (1–2 paragraphs)
  3. Writing sample (legal or academic)
  4. Availability (hours per week and preferred term)

About FASD United

FASD United is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing awareness, research, policy, and support for individuals and families affected by Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders. Through its Justice initiatives, FASD United works to improve legal system responses and outcomes for individuals with FASD.

Salary: Unpaid / Academic Credit Eligible

Job Description

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

We are the Clinical Trials Division (CTD): We Supply the Hope that Changes Lives

CTD partners with pharmaceutical and biotech customers around the world to ensure the right patients get the right therapies in the right doses at the right time - a concept that we internally embrace as "There is a Patient Waiting." Our unique blend of services includes project management, packaging, distribution, transportation management and specialty logistics, ancillary supply management, clinical supply optimization, bio-repository storage and much more. Our more than 4000 employees in over 15 countries work hard every day knowing that what they do matters. Thermo Fisher Scientific – Digital Solutions develops scalable digital and data capabilities that connect customer needs, business priorities, and technology delivery. This role partners across product, engineering, data, and business teams to deliver trusted solutions and measurable value.

Your Role in that Mission:

The Sr. Manager, Digital Product Solutions serves as a customer-facing link between customers, the IT organization, and engineering teams. The role leads customer discovery to understand business objectives, workflows, challenges, and product needs, then translates those insights into clear, actionable product and technical requirements. This role maintains and prioritizes a structured product backlog, identifies recurring needs across customers and market segments, and partners with IT and engineering leaders to deliver scalable capabilities that create measurable customer and business value.

Key Responsibilities:

Customer Discovery & Product Definition

· Build trusted customer relationships and lead discovery sessions, workshops, interviews, and workflow reviews to understand goals, pain points, business processes, and desired outcomes.

· Distinguish underlying customer needs from requested features and translate them into business requirements, use cases, functional and technical specifications, user stories, data/integration requirements, and acceptance criteria.

· Validate requirements and proposed solutions with customers and technical teams, resolving ambiguity throughout design and development while avoiding unnecessary one-off customization.

Backlog & Roadmap Management

· Create, maintain, and continuously refine a structured backlog of customer and product requirements.

· Synthesize requests across customers, industries, use cases, and segments; identify common themes and reusable solutions.

· Prioritize requirements using customer impact, strategic alignment, revenue potential, urgency, effort, risk, and applicability, and partner with product leadership and engineering to incorporate priorities into roadmaps and release plans.

· Communicate priorities, tradeoffs, dependencies, and expected timelines clearly to internal and external stakeholders.

Customer & Market Insights

· Analyze customer feedback and usage patterns to identify recurring problems, unmet needs, emerging opportunities, and differences across customer segments.

· Share structured customer insights with IT, engineering, sales, customer success, implementation, and leadership teams to inform product strategy and planning.

· Combine direct customer feedback with business priorities, product vision, and technical considerations to shape scalable product capabilities.

Cross-Functional Delivery & Enablement

· Partner with engineering, IT, customer experience, security, data, and commercial, global client services, to assess feasibility, dependencies, risks, and implementation options.

· Serve as the product representative in strategic customer discussions, roadmap reviews, and solution-design sessions, facilitating alignment when requirements or priorities conflict.

· Support product launches through documentation, enablement materials, release communications, and customer-facing presentations, ensuring capabilities and limitations are represented accurately.

As Demonstrated By:

· Customer empathy and consultative communication with strong stakeholder-management and facilitation skills.

· Structured requirements analysis, systems/process thinking, and technical aptitude.

· Product judgment, commercial awareness, and evidence-based prioritization in environments with competing priorities.

· Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and executive-level communication skills.

· Ability to navigate ambiguity, influence cross-functionally, and translate between business and technical audiences.

Key Requirements:

Education:

· Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Product Management, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

· Advanced degree or relevant product/Agile certification preferred.


Experience:

About SERVISS

At SERVISS, we deliver cutting-edge cybersecurity and IT solutions to government and commercial clients, with a mission to secure systems, data, and critical infrastructure through innovation and expertise. As we expand our capabilities, we’re seeking a hands-on CAASM engineer with Armis expertise to help build, integrate, and operate enterprise cyber asset visibility platforms.

Position Summary

SERVISS is seeking a CAASM Engineer to support the design, deployment, integration, and operation of Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management (CAASM) platforms — with a primary focus on Armis (Axonius or equivalent a plus) — across hybrid cloud and enterprise environments. The ideal candidate works as part of a cross-functional security team to onboard asset sources, streamline data pipelines, and enhance visibility into enterprise cyber assets, exposures, and risk. This position is scoped at a mid-level baseline (3+ years), but we actively encourage senior and highly experienced engineers to apply — role scope, level, and compensation can flex to match demonstrated expertise.

The Work

This is a hands-on engineering role. The selected candidate will:
  • Deploy, configure, and tune Armis (or equivalent CAASM platforms) across hybrid cloud and enterprise environments
  • Onboard and maintain data integrations from CMDBs, EDR/XDR, vulnerability feeds, cloud inventories, identity, network, and SaaS sources
  • Develop and maintain automation scripts and workflow connectors (Python, PowerShell, Bash) to enhance data ingestion and normalization
  • Build normalization, correlation, and enrichment logic that turns raw telemetry into authoritative asset intelligence
  • Monitor data quality, troubleshoot integration issues, and resolve engineering escalations
  • Support platform optimization, performance tuning, and operational stability
  • Configure dashboards, reports, and risk views that render asset and exposure data for technical and stakeholder audiences
  • Produce and maintain documentation for deployment architectures, configuration baselines, and operational procedures

Key Responsibilities

  • Assist with installation, configuration, and integration of CAASM platforms (Armis primary; Axonius or equivalent a plus)
  • Onboard and maintain data integrations from CMDBs, vulnerability feeds, cloud inventories, and endpoint tools
  • Develop and maintain automation scripts and workflow connectors to enhance data ingestion and normalization
  • Support CAASM platform optimization, performance tuning, and operational stability
  • Monitor data quality, troubleshoot integration issues, and resolve engineering escalations
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity analysts and stakeholders to translate security requirements into technical solutions
  • Support cyber governance reporting, continuous monitoring, and compliance automation efforts

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: 3+ years in cybersecurity engineering, systems integration, or IT infrastructure roles (candidates with more experience are encouraged to apply)
  • Hands-on experience with Armis, or a comparable CAASM / asset intelligence platform (e.g., Axonius)
  • Strong understanding of IT systems including Windows, Linux, and cloud platforms (AWS/Azure)
  • Familiarity with APIs, data ingestion pipelines, RESTful integration, and scripting (Python, PowerShell, Bash)
  • Knowledge of networking fundamentals and security principles (asset discovery, vulnerability context, normalization)
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or a similar field — or equivalent experience or relevant certifications

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct hands-on Armis deployment, integration, or administration experience
  • Experience with asset management, CAASM applications, or enterprise security tools
  • Familiarity with cloud-native services (AWS, Azure) and service APIs
  • Experience with SIEMs common in the federal market (e.g., Elastic, Splunk) and common sensor tools
  • Understanding of Federal cyber governance — NIST 800-53/171, RMF, CDM, and continuous monitoring
  • Certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GSEC, or vendor-specific CAASM certifications
  • Exposure to data analytics or BI dashboards related to security telemetry
  • Prior DoD or Federal civilian cybersecurity experience and an active security clearance

Freedom to Thrive.

Our goal as an employer is simple yet profound: to create an environment where you can be your best self, pursue your passions, and enjoy the freedom to thrive both personally and professionally. Your success is our success, and we’re committed to supporting you every step of the way.

  1. Investigates, evaluates and brings to timely resolution an inventory of low to moderately complex general liability claims of which some are litigated and may involve large property damage, bodily injury, inland marine and a sub- set of construction defect type claims in accordance with established claim handling standards and applicable state regulations and laws.
  2.   3. Composes a variety of other written communications to insureds, claimants, attorneys and agents in a professional and error-free manner.
  4. Understands and interprets construction contracts and apply risk transfer when appropriate.
  5. Evaluates and documents damages to ensure accurate and timely reserves; immediately escalate to management cases with potential exposure above your authority.
  6. Negotiates effectively and in good faith to achieve fair and accurate claim settlements.
  7. Manages litigated claim files proactively from inception to closure, including collaboration with defense counsel to determine and execute an appropriate plan of action; bring litigated cases to resolution either by negotiated settlement or trial, as appropriate.
  8. Negotiates the duty to defend and indemnify with liable insurers when appropriate.
  9. Retains experts and vendors to achieve appropriate claim outcomes while remaining mindful of loss adjustment expenses.
  10. Manages assigned workloads effectively to achieve quality and quantity production goals while providing superior customer service.
  11. Implements strategies to expeditiously close files and manages claims to a conclusion in the most effective manner possible.
  12. Documents all notes and file activity in a paperless claim system appropriately and clearly; compose detailed periodic reports including claim summary reports and large loss notifications, as needed.
  13. Communicates with other departments regarding developments on specific claim files as well as overall claim trends.

Focal Systems is the industry leader in retail AI solutions. We are headquartered in San Francisco, California with operations in Canada and the UK, and a tech-hub in Poland. Focal Systems has been deployed at scale with some of the top retailers in the world.

We seek smart, creative and passionate people who want to help build a great and enduring company and deploy Deep Learning to the world!

About the Role

As Director of Operations, UK you will help build and lead the field operations team that installs and maintains Focal Systems shelf cameras across our UK retail partners. Our cameras are being deployed at scale, with 100,000+ units live or rolling out at leading retailers around the world, and the UK is a major part of that growth.

You will work closely with senior and executive leadership to set and roll out operational strategy, and with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to make every deployment faster, more reliable, and more cost-effective than the last.

You will be joining an established, experienced team that works in cycles. Retailer rollouts bring periods of rapid scale-up, followed by quieter maintenance periods where we scale back down, and those transitions have not always been smooth. A key part of this role is making them smoother: planning ahead for each change in pace, keeping the team steady and supported through it, and building processes that let us ramp up and down without losing quality or momentum.

This is a senior leadership role. You will develop our existing team, support during scale-up and scale-down periods, set the operating rhythm for field work, and be the person our customers and colleagues rely on when something needs to get done.

  • You hire well, coach well, and build teams that take ownership without needing to be chased
  • You understand that operations is a customer-facing function, and you take pride in exceeding what our retail partners expect
  • You thrive in a fast-moving, remote-first environment and are energised by building something new

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own ongoing field-service performance and SLA delivery, prioritising maintenance work and driving issues through to resolution.
  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing UK field operations team responsible for installing and maintaining shelf cameras at scale
  • Own the operational plan for UK deployments, from scheduling and logistics through installation, quality checks, and ongoing maintenance
  • Define, track, and report on the key metrics for field performance and SLA adherence
  • Partner with executive leadership to set performance goals, budgets, and long-term operational strategy for the UK
  • Analyse operational processes end to end, identify bottlenecks, and lead improvements that increase speed, quality, and efficiency
  • Work across Product, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Customer Success to feed field insights back into hardware, software, and deployment playbooks
