As an Associate in Houlihan Capital’s Valuation and Financial Advisory practice, you will be an integral part of a high-performing team focused on delivering high-quality financial analyses and reports for a diverse range of client valuation needs, including Fair Value Measurement, Financial Reporting, Fair Market Value, Tax Reporting, and Transaction Opinions.

The position provides a unique opportunity to utilize valuation techniques across all types of illiquid investments (including debt, preferred equity, common equity, options, crypto assets, structured products, and more) across a wide variety of industries for private equity funds, venture capital funds, corporations, and many other clients.

Responsibilities:

  • Populate Excel-based valuation models used to value equity, debt, and other illiquid securities for financial reporting, tax, and transaction-related purposes.
    • Review, understand, and synthesize client-provided materials such as financial data, operating agreements, transaction documents, company presentations, and other essential documents.
    • Assist in drafting client presentations and reports, preparing supporting tables, charts, and exhibits that communicate findings.
    • Produce high-quality financial analyses including operating model builds, pro forma capitalization structures, and sensitivity analyses
    • Conduct research on industry trends, market conditions, and company-specific issues that will help client analyses.
    • Work closely with internal team members and clients on multiple engagements to ensure alignment on objectives.
    • Update the project manager on progress toward completion, client-provided information gaps, analytical challenges, and key assumptions.
  • Effectively prioritize tasks across multiple, simultaneous engagements, ensuring tight deadlines are consistently met without compromising quality.
  • Adapt to shifting priorities and manage competing demands by maintaining organized workflows, anticipating bottlenecks, and proactively communicating progress with team members and clients.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required. Preferred majors include Finance, Accounting, and Economics.
    • MBA preferred; CFA, or other relevant professional designation viewed favorably.
    • 1-2 years of relevant work experience in performing valuations for financial reporting or tax purposes.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex financial concepts in a clear and engaging way.
    • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint is required. Experience with financial databases like S&P Capital IQ, Pitchbook, or Bloomberg is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks, manage simultaneous engagements, and work independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • A keen eye for detail, particularly in reviewing financial and legal documents.

jobs.title: Director of Partnerships and Strategic Initiatives
jobs.excerpt: WHO WE ARE American Oversight (AO) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit watchdog that advances truth, accountability, and democracy by enforcing the public’s right to government records.
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

American Oversight (AO) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit watchdog that advances truth, accountability, and democracy by enforcing the public’s right to government records. We use multiple tools, backed by aggressive litigation, to fight attacks on democratic institutions, threats to civil rights and liberties, abuses of power, and the erosion of government transparency. We expose and disrupt these attacks — and the officials and networks behind them — by forcing the government to turn over records officials would rather keep secret.

Since our founding in 2017, American Oversight has worked on issues that touch nearly every aspect of American life. Our team has:

  • Secured a court order to preserve records in the 2025 “Signalgate” scandal, and spurred a related investigation by the Department of Defense inspector general that found Secretary Pete Hegseth had put troops’ lives in danger and violated federal recordkeeping laws.
  • Forced DOGE to implement a records preservation policy to ensure long-term accountability for its chaotic actions.
  • Revealed the Trump-sanctioned pressure campaign on the Ukrainian government by forcing the Trump administration to turn over records initially withheld from Congress.
  • Unmasked sham “audits” of the 2020 election in Wisconsin and Arizona, which used taxpayer money to undermine state elections.
  • Exposed the Trump administration’s unprecedented use of personal data to target immigrant communities and remove people from state voter rolls.

We are committed to fighting threats to democracy at the federal, state, and local levels, using time-tested and innovative tools to expose misconduct, defend against attacks on marginalized communities, and demand accountability.

For more information, please visit our website:

JOB OVERVIEW

The Director of Partnerships and Strategic Initiatives is a key member of American Oversight’s leadership team, responsible for shaping and executing the organization’s vision for partnerships and external engagement. The Director identifies, initiates, and cultivates strategic relationships that expand American Oversight’s influence and position it as the nation’s leading public records watchdog.

The Director builds and sustains mission-aligned partnerships that strengthen American Oversight’s sustainability and amplify its long-term impact across the progressive movement. By ensuring that the organization’s investigative findings and records reach partners, coalitions, policymakers, and other stakeholders best positioned to act on them, the Director helps translate American Oversight’s work into broader policy impact and systemic change.

Internally, the Director works closely with executive leadership and the Development team, and collaborates across the legal, communications, editorial, and investigations teams to ensure the organization’s work achieves maximum reach, strategic coordination, and measurable impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES (including but not limited to)

Partnerships and External Engagement

  • Direct American Oversight’s partnerships and external engagement strategy to expand the organization’s influence and cement American Oversight as the go-to authority on the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and public records work across the progressive movement at the federal, state, and local levels.
  • Strengthen American Oversight’s reputation as a trusted leader in government transparency, using strategic partnerships to identify high-impact investigations, litigation, and communications strategies designed to expose misconduct, expand public access to information, drive accountability, and support democratic progress.
  • Set and lead American Oversight’s strategic partnership priorities, building relationships with organizations whose complementary strengths, networks, and connections to impacted communities advance shared goals and broaden collective impact.
  • Proactively monitor and analyze political and policy dynamics at the federal, state, and local levels, cultivating partner insights to surface emerging threats and opportunities that guide American Oversight’s strategic direction and advance democratic accountability.
  • Develop and lead coalition-based strategies that leverage American Oversight’s expertise and records to shape accountability efforts, advance advocacy campaigns, and defend democratic institutions — including by drafting or supporting sign-on letters, joint statements, and other collaborative initiatives that amplify collective advocacy and align with American Oversight’s strategic priorities.
  • Facilitate webinars, presentations, and other public-facing engagements that showcase American Oversight’s findings, elevate the organization’s expertise, and strengthen relationships with partners, policymakers, and funders.
  • Elevate American Oversight’s visibility and influence across the accountability and democracy ecosystem by identifying, recommending, and securing opportunities for organizational leadership to participate in high-impact conferences, coalitions, and convenings that enhance the organization’s reputation and amplify its impact.
  • Advise executive leadership on strategic positioning within the broader progressive and democracy ecosystem, including assessing and managing potential risks in partnerships and coalitions.
  • Serve as American Oversight’s senior representative to external partners, coalitions, and public forums, advancing the organization’s mission, amplifying its priorities, and strengthening its credibility and influence across the accountability ecosystem.
Strategic Operations and Leadership
  • Translate broad organizational priorities into actionable partnership and strategic initiative plans, establishing milestones, coordinating internal contributions, and taking responsibility for execution and follow-through.
  • Define and track key performance metrics to evaluate the reach, influence, and effectiveness of American Oversight’s strategic engagement, ensuring accountability for outcomes and progress toward strategic goals.
  • Oversee American Oversight’s Client Relationship Management and Partnerships systems to ensure data hygiene, efficient information flow, and measurable tracking of partnerships growth and external engagement impact.
  • Build organizational capacity for external engagement by coaching and training staff across departments to effectively represent American Oversight in partnerships, coalitions, and public forums.
  • Coach and mentor direct report(s) by setting clear performance expectations, providing regular feedback, and supporting skills development and professional growth to strengthen individual and team effectiveness.
  • Other duties as assigned.
Development and Fundraising
  • Support American Oversight’s development and sustainability efforts by collaborating with executive leadership to design, execute, and sustain fundraising strategies, engage funders, and cultivate relationships.
  • Collaborate with the Development and Communications teams to translate American Oversight’s partnerships, impact, and investigations into compelling narratives that inspire donor engagement and investment.
  • Assist with or draft grant and impact reports, as well as other funder-facing materials, that communicate American Oversight’s achievements and reinforce relationships with institutional supporters.
  • Ensure alignment between external engagement initiatives and development priorities, leveraging partnerships, events, and visibility opportunities to advance fundraising goals and institutional relationships.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

  • 10+ years of experience in nonprofit, advocacy, or related settings, including substantial experience working in or closely with 501(c)(3) advocacy, community-based, or watchdog organizations, and a demonstrated record of building strategic partnerships that advance shared goals.
    • 5+ years of experience advancing government accountability through advocacy, oversight, transparency, or related work.
    • 3+ years of experience directly managing early-career staff, including setting performance expectations, providing regular feedback, and fostering professional growth through mentorship and coaching.
  • Strong working knowledge of the nonprofit advocacy landscape, including the role of 501(c)(3) and (c)(4) organizations, democracy organizations and coalitions, and how national, state, and community organizations collaborate to advance shared goals.
  • Demonstrated experience building a program, initiative, or partnership strategy from the ground up, including identifying opportunities, securing participation, and carrying the work through to measurable results.
  • Experience delivering results in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities, including responding to emerging opportunities, managing competing deadlines, and independently advancing work with limited direction.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders and communicate organizational impact through persuasive narratives that advance strategic objectives and influence decision-makers.
  • Exceptionally strong skills in the following:
    • Relationship Cultivation: Demonstrated ability to build and sustain strategic, high-trust partnerships with advocacy groups, community organizations, senior government officials, policymakers, and funders. Confident and proactive in initiating contact with senior leaders, making clear requests, and turning introductions into substantive collaboration. Skilled at navigating sensitive dynamics, exercising discretion, and leveraging relationships to advance election integrity, civil rights, and democratic accountability.
    • Project Management: Sets priorities and strategies across multiple projects with varying timelines; manages high volumes of correspondence with internal and external stakeholders; and anticipates next steps to align expectations and outcomes. Maintains momentum through timely follow-up, clear ownership, and proactive resolution of obstacles.
    • Communication: Synthesizes and conveys complex ideas clearly and effectively across formats and audiences. Distills technical or nuanced information into accessible, compelling content. Provides strong editing support and helps team members strengthen communication for strategic alignment.
    • Judgment and Decision-Making: Makes sound, well-reasoned decisions, leading the Partnerships Department to highly impactful outcomes, including strong partnerships; responds to and addresses concerns or challenges appropriately and in a timely manner.
    • Problem Solving and Critical Thinking: Identifies issues and surfaces creative solutions to achieve desired outcomes; processes large volumes of complex information, discerns meaningful patterns, and draws well-reasoned conclusions.
    • Collaboration: Entrepreneurial in cultivating relationships, with deep experience engaging diverse stakeholders and coalitions. Facilitates strong internal cross-component collaboration. Brings self-motivation, collegiality, and the ability to thrive both collaboratively and independently.
  • Self-starter with demonstrated good judgment, critical thinking, flexibility, resourcefulness, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Exceptional organizational skills, discipline, and attention to detail with experience multitasking and managing several projects with varying scopes, timelines, or stakeholders.
  • Quick learner, able to rapidly build fluency across diverse issue areas and apply that knowledge to advance strategic goals.
  • Experience working in and/or desire to contribute to workplaces with a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, including a demonstrated commitment to coaching of entry and mid-level staff members.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Established relationships with leaders in nonprofit advocacy, community organizations, national watchdogs, or related coalitions that could support American Oversight’s partnership goals.
  • Deep understanding of the accountability and democracy ecosystem, including organizations, funders, and coalitions working to strengthen transparency, oversight, and civic participation at the federal and state levels.
  • Knowledge of government transparency and accountability frameworks, including familiarity with FOIA or related state-level open records laws.
  • Experience contributing to organizational planning and strategic initiatives, particularly those involving cross-departmental collaboration, external positioning, or long-term sustainability.
  • Experience working in an advocacy organization that includes litigation as a primary tactic.
  • Experience positively navigating through change management.
  • Development experience either with philanthropic organizations and/or donor cultivation.

COMPENSATION

The salary range for this position is $125,000–$150,000, commensurate with experience.

BENEFITS

  • Remote-first work environment
  • Medical, dental and vision insurance
  • Generous paid time off
  • Paid office closure from Christmas Eve to New Years’ Day
  • 403(b) with up to 4% employer match
  • Flexible scheduling policy aligned with core business hours
  • Summer Fridays
  • Up to $100/month reimbursement for internet services and personal device
  • Professional development stipend
  • $400/yr home office stipend
  • Commuter benefits

LOCATION

Position is located in the United States; must be available to work East Coast business hours with occasional evening and weekend hours, as needed.

TIMELINE

Interested applicants are encouraged to apply by Wednesday, November 4 to ensure consideration of their application. Following this deadline, we will be interviewing candidates and continue to review applications on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Senior Recruiter, NA & EMEA

Location: This job may be fully remote or a hybrid position in Wayne, PA, or Atlanta, GA. Candidates on the East Coast are preferred.


Annual base salary range is 95K - 113K USD.


Interested in a career that bridges the gap between Supply Chain and Technology?

Elemica, an award-winning digital supply chain SaaS company, is seeking an experienced Senior Recruiter to lead Talent Acquisition across North America and EMEA. Join a growing team committed to exceeding client expectations.


Our Values


At Elemica, we believe that embodying our values is essential for all team members. These qualities show up in our interactions with each other, our clients, and our collective community:

  • Curiosity – we delight in the discovery of new challenges and feel compelled to solve them
  • Integrity – We are relatable and trustworthy; steadfast in our commitment to our colleagues, clients, and partners
  • Accountability – We show up and deliver measurable, meaningful business value. Consistently.
  • Passion – We have a shared enthusiasm for transforming our clients’ supply chain

What’s In It For You?


  • Unlimited Paid Flexible Time Off Policy
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents and careers
  • Health & Voluntary/Pet Insurance Options
  • Retirement savings and bonus programs
  • Employee engagement events
  • Wellness Initiatives
  • Generous Employee Referral Program
  • Global, hybrid/remote work environment

Role & Responsibilities


The Senior Recruiter develops and executes global recruiting strategy for a private equity-backed SaaS organization, partnering with HR Business Partners, Executives, and Senior Business Leaders across North America and EMEA. This highly visible role combines strategic leadership with hands-on ownership of the full recruiting lifecycle, operations, technology, vendors, reporting, and candidate experience.

Core Talent Acquisition Responsibilities

  • Manage the full recruiting lifecycle from requisition intake through candidate acceptance and onboarding handoff, including revenue-generating roles
  • Engage passive candidates through direct sourcing, networking, referrals, and targeted outreach
  • Screen candidates for qualifications, capabilities, cultural alignment, overall fit, and compensation expectations; coordinate complex, multi-region interview processes

Senior-Level Recruiting

  • Lead senior-level and occasional executive searches across commercial, professional services, product, marketing, finance, legal, technology, engineering, IT, and other corporate functions
  • Conduct confidential searches and protect sensitive candidate information

Hiring Manager Partnership

  • Serve as the strategic Talent Acquisition advisor to hiring managers and executive leaders
  • Provide regular search updates to hiring managers and executive leaders
  • Reinforce expectations for timely interview feedback and hiring decisions

Recruiting Operations

  • Manage requisition creation, approval, prioritization, tracking, and closure across business functions
  • Track recruiting activity, pipeline health, aging requisitions, and hiring progress

ATS & Recruiting Technology

  • Administer and optimize Workday ATS technology, integrations, and enhancements
  • Partner with internal and external resources on workflow design, testing, communications, implementation, and process improvement
  • Standardize system processes and automate repetitive recruiting activities where practical

Recruiting Process Design

  • Build and optimize standardized end-to-end recruiting processes that reduce unnecessary steps and delays
  • Create consistent frameworks for candidate screening, interview scheduling, communication, evaluation, and feedback

Candidate Experience

  • Provide clear, timely, and professional communication to every candidate, regardless of hiring outcome

Sourcing & Talent Pipeline Development

  • Develop sourcing strategies and campaigns for difficult-to-fill roles using LinkedIn Recruiter and other channels
  • Maintain evergreen pipelines for recurring and strategically important roles

Agency & Vendor Management

  • Manage external search partners, determine when agency support is appropriate, and negotiate contracts, fees, terms, and service expectations
  • Build internal sourcing capabilities to reduce unnecessary agency dependence

Global Recruiting

  • Develop recruiting approaches that reflect regional talent markets, candidate expectations, and requirements
  • Coordinate interviews across time zones and partner with stakeholders in Germany, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands while maintaining consistent global processes

Employer Brand & Talent Attraction

  • Partner with Marketing on social media posts, calendar, and strategy
  • Develop compelling candidate messages that communicate the company's mission, culture, products, technology, growth opportunities, and employee value proposition to candidates
  • Create and brand job descriptions

Offer Management & Closing

  • Develop competitive and compelling offers in partnership with Finance, HRBPs, and hiring managers/budget owners
  • Create and understand employment contracts for Germany, The Netherlands, and The United Kingdom and employment offers for the United States
  • Present and explain offers to candidates, negotiate compensation and other employment terms within established parameters

What You’ll Need


Basic Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive Talent Acquisition experience, including executive recruiting or recruiting leadership
  • Experience recruiting revenue-generating Account Executives and other critical go-to-market roles across North America and EMEA
  • Demonstrated success independently managing full-cycle recruiting and passive candidate sourcing
  • In-house recruiting experience within a SaaS, technology, software, or B2B company
  • Experience advising senior executives and recruiting across multiple corporate functions
  • Proficiency with Workday ATS operations, recruiting processes, interview frameworks, metrics, and reporting
  • Experience managing agencies and vendors
  • Ability to manage concurrent searches and competing priorities during organizational transformation

Preferred Experience

  • Private equity-backed or sponsor-backed company experience
  • Demonstrated understanding of the digital supply chain industry, including key market trends, technologies, and solutions that drive supply chain visibility, connectivity, automation, and operational efficiency
  • Experience recruiting technical Product, Engineering, and Technology talent
  • Experience developing global recruiting programs
  • Experience reducing recruiting costs and external agency dependence

Leadership Attributes

  • Strategic, commercially minded recruiter who moves fluidly between planning and hands-on search execution
  • Highly organized, data-driven, consultative, and influential without relying on formal authority
  • Exceptional communicator and relationship builder who works effectively with executives and frontline hiring managers
  • Responsive and adaptable in a fast-paced private equity environment
  • Comfortable constructively challenging stakeholders

Who We Are

Elemica is a leading provider of Digital Supply Chain Management solutions and the premier multi-enterprise collaboration network for global process manufacturing industries. Its portfolio of SaaS-based, network-powered digitization and visibility solutions automate critical information flows, enable multi-channel data strategies, and improve end-to-end supply chain performance. Elemica solutions connect many of the world’s largest manufacturers to their direct material suppliers, logistics service providers and end customers, helping them realize the promise of, and return on, their investments in supply chain digitization. Today, global leaders—including Arkema, BASF, Continental, Dow, Goodyear, Michelin, and Shell—use Elemica, driving over $1 trillion in commerce annually.


All Elemica employees are responsible for safeguarding the security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy of company and customer systems and data. Employees must follow a security-first approach and protect their devices, work areas, and communications.

Our use of artificial intelligence in hiring.


We use AI-assisted tools to support parts of our recruitment process. These tools help us manage application volume, but no hiring decision is made by AI alone. You may also request information about how AI was used in evaluating your candidacy and contest any decision that was influenced by automated processing. jobs.description:
Job Summary:

The mission of the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is to advance the public's health through learning, discovery and communication. To pursue the mission, the school produces knowledge through research then translates this knowledge into evidence that can be communicated to the public, policymakers, and practitioners to advance the health of populations.

The Office of Sponsored Programs Administration (SPA) supports the School's mission by serving as a central resource for the research community through the provision of expertise and leadership in obtaining and managing research funds. It acts as the institutional representative of the President and Fellows of Harvard College for the administration of sponsored projects for the school. SPA is comprised of research administrators that work in partnership with faculty to review and submit proposals for funding and to ensure that proposals and then awards conform and are managed according to sponsor guidelines and University policies.

The Associate Director of Finance (ADF) supports innovative research at the world’s leading public health research institution, working across the Department of Environmental Health and the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies (HCPDS). The Department of Environmental Health advances environmental health through hands-on learning, evidence -based research, and translation of discoveries into actions that reduce harmful exposures and improve health, with longstanding strengths in the epidemiology of cancer, cardiovascular, and other chronic diseases. It also educates and prepares future medical and public health leaders. Administered by the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies (HCPDS) brings together scientists from across the University to make critical advances in population research. With over 70 affiliated faculty from the Kennedy School of Government, the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, the Medical School, and other schools, HCPDS is a University-wide, interdisciplinary center dedicated to understanding how demographic change and social and physical environments shape global population health.

The Associate Director of Finance is a key departmental leader responsible for overall financial and grants management. This role supervises a team of financial staff, including grant managers and accounts payable personnel. The position reports to the Director of Finance, Administration, and Compliance in Sponsored Programs Administration, with joint reporting lines to the Director of Administration (EH) and the Deputy Director (HCPDS).

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

The Associate Director of Finance is an integral part of the research enterprise and works in close partnership with faculty members to advise them on the financial management of their funds and will have oversight over the Department's sponsored research portfolio as well as their non sponsored funds.

The responsibilities of the ADF include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Team Management
    • Supervising and training research and financial administrators; providing daily guidance
    • Allocating workloads to maximize research administrator effectiveness
    • Assessing performance and conducting reviews for staff
    • Serving as a resource for Grants Managers by assisting them in interpreting Harvard, School and sponsor policies, regulations, and procedures
    • Having overall responsibility for the management of non-sponsored funding, including gifts and endowments
  • Oversight of Department’s Sponsored Research
    • Overseeing pre- and post-award management for a large portfolio of sponsored research grants and subcontracts, a large portion of which is from the NIH
    • Providing guidance to the faculty, ensuring they have the information they need to effectively and compliantly manage their funding and effort
    • Developing and implementing departmental policies and processes
    • Ensuring research administration compliance with sponsor guidelines and Harvard policies
    • Ensuring departmental financial transactions are compliant with Harvard and sponsor policies and regulations; approves and transmits most departmental transactions.
  • Strategic and Financial Leadership
    • Oversight and management of the department’s non-sponsored accounts. These include but are not limited to endowments, gifts, start-up funding, and cost recovery centers
    • Collaborates with departments academic staff regarding student finances and financial planning
    • Preparing annual Department budget, working closely with the Department Administrator and senior leadership
    • Working closely with senior management, including the Director of Administration, Department Chair, and Directors of educational programs and student services, in developing and implementing strategic financial plans
    • Participating in School-wide and University-wide initiatives and meetings
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required
  • Minimum of 7 years’ relevant work experience
  • Advanced knowledge of sponsored research regulations
  • Supervisory experience

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

  • MBA or Masters’ degree in relevant field
  • CRA certification
  • Strong computing skills, particularly with Microsoft Excel and Word
  • Experience with Microsoft Office Suite, advanced Excel skills
  • Knowledge of advanced financial principles, budget management, financial analysis
  • Expert knowledge of federal sponsored research policies and regulations strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with international projects
  • Education and/or experience with general finance and accounting concepts and practices
  • Knowledge of Harvard systems including GMAS, HART, Buy2Pay, and Concur
  • Knowledge of human subject use, animal use and other research compliance areas
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Effective interpersonal skills
  • Experience working with faculty and students
  • Effectively assesses priorities, manages change, and effectively juggles multiple complex activities in a time-sensitive environment.
  • Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
  • Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
  • Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education, Criminal, Credit

Join the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health to support our mission of health research and education, and to be a part of the oldest institution of higher learning in the country!

  • The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health does not provide visa sponsorship, now or in the future, for staff positions.

  • Harvard University requires pre-employment reference checks and background screenings.

  • This position has a 90 day orientation and review period.

The health of our workforce is a priority for Harvard University. With that in mind, we strongly encourage all employees to be up to date on CDC-recommended vaccines.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that the duties and responsibilities can effectively be performed fully remotely at a non-Harvard location. Employees in fully remote positions must work all scheduled hours in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. At the discretion of the department, fully remote employees may occasionally be required on site at a Harvard location. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 058. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Generous paid time off including parental leave
  • Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one
  • Retirement plans with university contributions
  • Wellbeing and mental health resources
  • Support for families and caregivers
  • Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement
  • Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.

EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes.

Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy. Harvard's equal employment opportunity policy and non-discrimination policy help all community members participate fully in work and campus life free from harassment and discrimination.

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health?

The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is a world-renowned institution dedicated to advancing public health through cutting-edge research, education, and global collaboration. Our school is a special place to work because of its vibrant, mission-driven community, interdisciplinary approach, and commitment to addressing some of the most pressing health challenges worldwide. We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where innovation, continuous learning, and work-life balance are valued.

Learn more about the School’s mission, objectives, and core values, our Principles of Citizenship, and about the Dean’s AAA vision about our school’s ongoing strategic initiatives.

jobs.description:
Magna Legal Services is a trusted nationwide partner to law firms, corporations, insurance carriers, and government agencies, delivering comprehensive legal support at every stage of a case. From court reporting and record retrieval to jury consulting, investigations, litigation graphics, and language services, we help our clients navigate complex legal challenges with confidence. Our reputation is built on the expertise, dedication, and professionalism of our team, and we’re proud to foster a culture where talented people can do meaningful work and grow their careers.

About Magna

Magna Legal Services is a distributed business, and Microsoft 365 is how our people work: email, files, meetings, collaboration, and the security wrapped around all of it. When it works well, nobody notices. When it doesn't, work stops, and the people on the other end are professionals who need it fixed fast.

We're looking for a technology leader to take ownership of that platform — and the Azure cloud and infrastructure underneath it — and to lead and grow the people who keep it running.

Position overview

    You'll be accountable for the availability, security, and usefulness of Magna's IT systems, with Microsoft 365 at the center. That means owning the platform's strategy and roadmap, making sure it's secure and well governed, and making sure our people actually get value from it — not just that it's switched on.

    You'll partner with operations leadership to understand what the business needs, work with the VP of IT and Technology leadership to set priorities and policies, and coordinate with our Information Security Officer on data security and resiliency. You'll also oversee the Azure and infrastructure environments behind Microsoft 365 and our business-critical applications, and manage the vendors and partners we rely on.

    You'll lead a geographically distributed IT team, and a big part of your job is raising the level of the whole organization — developing your people, standardizing how we work, and leading by example.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, and day-to-day operation of Microsoft 365 — Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and other Applications — along with identity, security, and device management
  • Oversee the Azure cloud and core infrastructure that support Microsoft 365 and business-critical applications, working with our systems and cloud engineers
  • Partner with operations leadership to turn business needs into practical, cost-effective solutions
  • Work with the VP of IT and technology leadership to set priorities, policies, and standard operating procedures
  • Coordinate with the Information Security Officer to keep data secure and systems resilient
  • Manage relationships with IT vendors and partners, including Microsoft and managed service providers
  • Look for ways to add value, improve efficiency, and cut costs — including Microsoft 365 licensing and adoption
  • Develop and coach your team, and build standardized, documented, cross-trained ways of working
  • Keep end-user and technology support consistent across headquarters and our business units
  • Maintain accurate inventories of IT assets and licenses, and monitor compliance with regulatory and contractual requirements
  • Establish and maintain our disaster recovery and business continuity program for your areas of responsibility

Desired Background

    Required qualifications

  • 10+ years designing, supporting, deploying, and evolving technology platforms, infrastructure, and solutions
  • 5+ years managing diverse and rapidly evolving IT platforms and services
  • 5+ years of Microsoft platform management and administration, including Microsoft 365
  • 5+ years managing technology teams in a diverse, geographically distributed business
  • Deep knowledge of the Microsoft stack — SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Power BI, and Office desktop and mobile applications
  • Experience supporting Microsoft 365 users in a distributed, highly mobile business
  • Experience building and maintaining secure, highly available cloud environments (Azure; AWS a plus)
  • A proven ability to translate business requirements into solution strategies in partnership with senior business leaders
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication, and a collaborative style with peer IT leaders
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Information Sciences or a similar field, or equivalent experience

    • Preferred qualifications

  • Microsoft 365 or other Microsoft certifications
  • A deep understanding of the Azure / Microsoft 365 security model and group and policy structures
  • Experience with Intune/EMS, Purview information protection, Defender, and Entra ID
  • Experience moving on-premises systems to the cloud (Azure; AWS a plus)
  • Experience with data security standards and regulations relevant to the legal industry
  • Experience in a legal or regulated business environment, including handling highly secure and confidential client data

Key Characteristics

  • Ability to multitask using time management skills such as prioritizing, organizing, tracking details, and meeting deadlines on multiple projects with varying completion dates.
  • Mature and self-motivated professional able to work in a fast-paced and constantly changing environment.
  • Collaborative problem solver and solution champion.
  • Strong sense of intellectual curiosity and interest in understanding business objectives and how technology can be leveraged.
  • Passionate about creative, cost-effective solutions to business problems and opportunities.
  • Active engagement in and understanding of the business — as a partner and collaborator with operational management.
  • Capability to work as an effective and collaborative member of a distributed IT leadership team.
  • A keen focus on customer satisfaction and high-quality service delivery, with strong interpersonal skills, responsiveness, and outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

Job Title: Senior Systems Administrator & Architect

Department: Information Technology & Digital Security

Location: ​United States (Eastern time zone working hours) or Western/Central European time zone

Workspace Designation: Hybrid-Optional or Remote

Reports to Title: Senior Director, Information Technology & Digital Security

Closing Date: November 6th, 2026

Organization Overview:

Founded in 1981, the Committee to Protect Journalists (“CPJ”) is an independent, non-profit organization defending journalists worldwide without regard to their political ideology. Through its work to safeguard journalists, CPJ protects the rights of all people to have access to diverse and independent sources of information. For over four decades, CPJ has helped win the early release of imprisoned journalists, secure convictions in journalist murders, and enable legal reform in countries where free expression has deteriorated. CPJ’s widely cited database and reports have raised global awareness of attacks on press freedom. Learn more about CPJ’s fight to defend freedom of the press here

At CPJ, we are dedicated to upholding values of equity and free expression in both our internal operations and external endeavors. As a global organization headquartered in the United States, we aspire to build a diverse workplace and foster an inclusive and welcoming environment. We strive for our people to be representative of the global community on which we report and to equip them with the opportunities and resources they need to learn and succeed.

Job Summary:

CPJ is seeking a hands-on Senior Systems Administrator & Architect who pairs technical aptitude with a strong understanding of functional process design. Reporting to the Senior Director, Information Technology and Digital Security, the right candidate will join a small team that works closely with our Managed Service Provider (MSP)
and supports staff across many countries and time zones.

The primary focus of the role is administering, co-architecting, implementing solutions and supporting both our Salesforce-based data management and workflow system and our enterprise collaboration platforms, and may also be asked to support additional technology products while helping design enterprise data and process models to help inform the technical work within those systems. This is a builder and problem-solver role for someone who enjoys connecting systems, people, and processes.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Business Process & Documentation

  • Partner with stakeholders to map current-state processes and identify gaps or inefficiencies in systems
  • Translate business requirements into system solutions and clear functional designs
  • Create and maintain process documentation, system documentation, and user guides
  • Manage the Information technology change lifecycle: requirements, build, testing, rollout, and training
  • Serve as a go-to resource for system questions and provide user support and training

Information Architecture and Knowledge Management

  • Conduct user interviews, stakeholder sessions, usability tests, and sorting exercises to understand how target audiences group and search for information
  • Build structural blue-prints, flowcharts, and site maps that define how content and data are organized and accessed across platforms
  • Sketch low-fidelity wireframes and interactive mockups to show screen layouts, navigation paths, and user flows
  • Design clear naming conventions, category structures, and metadata tagging systems matching user mental models
  • Work alongside internal teams and development consultants to translate business goals into technology system solutions

Systems Administration:

  • Administer and configure core systems, including Salesforce and other cloud productivity and collaboration platforms such as Google Suite or Microsoft 365
  • Manage user access, roles, permissions, and security settings across platforms
  • Build and maintain workflows, automation, and validation logic within each system
  • Support integrations and data flows between systems, working with vendors or technical partners as needed
  • In collaboration with MSP, Monitor system health, troubleshoot issues, and coordinate resolution with vendors and consultants
  • Evaluate new tools, features, and releases for fit and impact
  • Maintain data quality through imports, cleanup, and governance practices
  • Build reports and dashboards that support operational and leadership decisions

Software/Hardware Asset Management and General Tech Support

  • General IT support and software/hardware asset management is provided via a MSP on a day-to-day basis. The successful candidate may be asked to assist with the following types of duties in surge capacity: hardware support, software management, ticket & incident handling, user accounts & security, network & connectivity, on- and off-boarding processes, asset inventory & tracking.

Qualifications & Competencies:

Required:

  • 3–5+ years supporting, administering and configuring multiple enterprise business systems (CRM, ERP, HRIS, Google Workspace, MS365, Salesforce and/or similar SaaS platforms)
  • Hands-on experience configuring workflows, automation, and permission models
  • Experience gathering requirements and turning them into system designs
  • Strong process mapping and documentation skills
  • Comfort working with data: imports/exports, cleanup, and basic reporting
  • Clear communicator who can explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
  • Organized, self-directed, and comfortable owning work end to end across multiple systems
  • Adaptability: Ability to adjust on the fly for shifting priorities
  • Experience supporting and guiding users on a variety of technology platforms
  • Aptitude and willingness to provide remote training
  • Communication: Ability to break down complex, technical concepts into simple, everyday language.
  • Patience and Empathy: A supportive and approachable demeanor when helping frustrated or non-technical users
  • Public Speaking: Confidence in presenting materials clearly and keeping an audience engaged
  • Organization: Strong time management to coordinate schedules, workload and priorities

Preferred:

  • Salesforce administration experience; Salesforce Certified Administrator a strong plus
  • Google Workspace Administration
  • Microsoft 365 administration experience including: Teams, Exchange, SharePoint and Entra ID
  • Experience with Power Automate, Flow or other low-code automation tools
  • Exposure to integrations, APIs, or middleware (e.g., Zapier, Workato, MuleSoft)
  • Familiarity with SQL or scripting
  • Relevant experience with process mapping tools (Lucidchart, Visio, or similar)
  • Background in Nonprofit Administration

Physical Requirements:

This position’s physical demands reflect work in a typical office setting. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Work Location:

This position is open to candidates within the United States or those located within the Western or Central European time zones, and is classified as remote, or hybrid-optional. Availability to work and attend meetings on the US Eastern time zone and to travel to New York for meetings as needed is required.

We promote a flexible working environment with hybrid and flexible work schedule opportunities. Our office is located in New York City office in midtown Manhattan, and was designed to be a place where we can work effectively and collaboratively, bringing energy, inspiration, commitment, and deep learning to our mission. Staff hired in the commutable NYC area are welcome and encouraged to use the CPJ office.

Benefits (subject to change):

Benefit packages are specific to the hiring location. More information can be provided as part of the interview process. If this position is hired outside of the United States, it will ultimately be managed by an Employer of Record (EOR) firm that is engaged by CPJ for the purpose of employing international staff. CPJ offers a comprehensive benefits package for US employees; benefits for staff hired through the EoR will be consistent with those that are standard in the country of hire.

jobs.excerpt: As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit.
jobs.description:
As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit. His fix was a card that let members eat now and pay later. That card became Diners Club, widely credited as the first multipurpose charge card. It was a piece of cardboard and a promise: the restaurant trusted the card, the card trusted the member, and someone had to make sure the money actually moved.

More than seventy-five years later, the promise hasn't changed, but the machinery has. When a Mercury customer taps their card, the request goes from the merchant's terminal through an acquirer and a card network to us. In a fraction of a second, we check the balance, apply the customer's spend controls, screen for fraud and say yes or no. After that comes clearing, settlement, disputes and reporting, and every cent has to reconcile.

Cards are the way Mercury customers spend money. The Cards Integration team owns the whole Mercury card, not just the swipe: issuance, physical card shipping, spend controls, lifecycle management, authorization, money movement, settlement and reporting, and the infrastructure underneath. We're a full-stack team, and our job is to make the Mercury Debit and IO cards reliable, correct, useful, and innovative.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who thinks deeply about systems architecture, cares about the customer experience, and will dive into any problem to move the team forward. We value high ownership, working in pairs and teams rather than alone, and attention to detail. Those matter when you run systems held to four nines of reliability, and everyone around you will care about them too.

In this role, you will

  • Lead projects from idea to tech spec to implementation to launch, working with your PM, EM, tech lead, and teammates at each stage. When you lead a project, it's yours to see through.
  • Learn how debit and credit cards actually work under the hood (authorization, clearing, settlement, disputes) and use that knowledge every day.
  • Build features across the stack, from the card experiences customers use to the backend systems that move money.
  • Help keep our operations excellent. Our systems are some of the most observable at Mercury, and with great observability comes great responsibility.
  • Mentor other engineers and raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and collaboration.
  • Work with product, design, operations, risk, compliance, sales, and many other teams.

You should

  • Have strong full-stack experience, a product mindset, systems thinking, and a knack for getting things across the line.
  • Have made architectural decisions on complex systems, and be able to explain your reasoning and the trade-offs.
  • Be excited to put new features in customers' hands, and care just as much about keeping existing ones working like a charm.
  • Care about correctness in systems where failure has real financial consequences.
  • Communicate clearly, handle ambiguity well, and enjoy mentoring others.
  • Be comfortable with our tech stack (Haskell and TypeScript) or be ready to learn.
  • Bonus: experience in fintech, payments, or card issuing.

We encourage you to try our demo site if you're interested in applying for the role.

jobs.description:
About the role

Health Log Analytics (HLA) ingests, stores, and analyzes the logs that power ServiceNow's AIOps suite. We want it to be the data backbone teams trust to find problems early and fix them fast.

HLA is a data platform for operational logs at high volume, built for ServiceNow’s large enterprise customers. The work spans the full data path: collection and ingestion, routing and enrichment, durable storage and retention, and fast, cost-aware query. Our ingest builds on OpenTelemetry, and we have our own Rust-based log storage. As data volume, customer needs, and AI-driven use cases grow, we need the platform to get more reliable, more efficient, and more useful.

We're looking for a senior technical leader to help set where HLA goes next. You'll work side by side with engineering and product leadership on the roadmap. You'll bring a clear point of view and show it with a prototype, not just a slide.

You'll set the technical bar for experienced engineers. You'll do it by being a great teammate, not the loudest person in the room.

What you'll do

  • Help shape the HLA roadmap with engineering, product, and leadership. Bring both vision and a reality check.
  • Work directly with customers to make sure HLA keeps delivering value as their needs change. Turn their feedback into clear, actionable input for product and the roadmap.
  • Set architecture direction across ingest, storage, and query, and across teams you don't own.
  • Write down your point of view, then build a prototype that helps others see it and get behind it.
  • Say no, with reasons. That includes AI ideas with no evidence behind them, and timelines or designs that don't fit today's constraints. Know when to push past those constraints, too.
  • Lead deep design reviews that raise the bar and leave people feeling sharper, not smaller.
  • Define the reliability and efficiency bar for the HLA data path: completeness, durability, latency, availability, tenant isolation, and unit cost.
  • Lead the technical approach to hard transitions, such as storage migrations, schema changes, replay, and upgrades with little or no downtime.
  • Set clear architectural boundaries and contracts for the teams building collection, ingest, storage, anomaly detection, query, and AIOps experiences.
  • Show how we build with AI. Weigh ideas against customer value, data quality, reliability, and cost. Run small experiments to help us decide what to scale.
  • Set the example on quality, on-call, and learning from incidents.
  • Mentor senior engineers and tech leads. Help grow the next technical leaders.
  • Work as a real partner to engineering and product leadership. Learn in the open.

To be successful in this role you have

  • Experience in leveraging or critical thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision making, or problem solving. This includes using AI powered tools, automated workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or reasoning about AI’s impact on how infrastructure is built and run.
  • 12+ years building and operating production distributed systems, with substantial ownership of large-scale data or platform systems. Equivalent depth shown through sustained technical leadership counts too.
  • Broad grounding across data ingestion, storage and query, and AI on top of data. Deep expertise in at least one.
  • Experience with ingest tools like Kafka, Pulsar, or Kinesis, and with columnar stores, time-series databases, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, or object-storage designs
  • A record of changing the direction of teams you didn't own, through credibility and clear thinking
  • Evidence-based judgment on AI. You know where it belongs and where it doesn’t, and you’ve built safeguards for correctness, safety, and cost. You’ve shipped with it, or you’re a strong proponent with a clear point of view.
  • Good judgment on tradeoffs: consistency, latency, cost, and operational burden
  • Comfort with Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure at scale
  • Fluency in at least one of Go, Java, Scala, Rust, or Python. You prototype and review deeply, and you write code when it counts.
  • Clear communication. You can explain a tricky design to a new hire or a VP and have both of them get it.

Nice to Have:

  • A background in observability, log analytics, OpenTelemetry or AIOps
  • Experience at an AI-native company, or building agents and LLM-based features
  • Experience with multitenant SaaS and per-tenant isolation

Who you are

  • Humble, smart, and you care about people
  • You have experience working remotely and leading remote teams
  • You make the people around you better, and you share the work and the credit
  • You're comfortable when the problem isn't fully defined, and you help define it
  • You turn small, messy things into big, solid ones
  • You care about the people who run what you build

Why join us

You'll work on real scale problems with real customers. You'll have room to shape the architecture and the direction of a product that matters. And you'll join a team that values clear thinking, honest feedback, and shipping.

At CapsLock, people, technology, and forward-thinking innovation lie at the heart of everything we do. Our diverse, global team, fluent in over 10 languages, thrives on open collaboration and the exchange of new ideas, pushing boundaries to ensure our clients' success.

Role overview

We're looking for a Marketing Design Team Lead who is equal parts creative leader, marketer, and AI geek, someone who knows how to achieve business goals through visuals that actually sell.

You will take a team of 3 AI-driven Creative Designers and scale it to 6. The team produces static ad creatives, photorealistic AI visuals for performance campaigns across paid media channels, and source assets for our video production pipeline.

Your job is to build the company's visual creative engine. Whatever the starting point- a brief, a hypothesis, a raw idea - it leaves the team as a creative that performs.

You'll work closely with Creative Producers, Marketers, Copywriters, Media Buyers, and the Video Editing team, and partner with our Generative AI Pipeline Engineer on tooling and workflows.

What you will work on

  • Lead, mentor, and scale a team of 3 to 6 AI-driven Creative Designers - grow people, not just output;
  • Own the production flow: task distribution, capacity planning, and strict QC - production-grade, not demo-grade;
  • Drive creative direction: concepts, hooks, and visual angles that stop the scroll and convert;
  • Generate ideas yourself and push the team beyond safe iterations - informed by visual trends and competitor creatives;
  • Own the creative testing loop: build a database of winners, analyze failures, turn performance data into next iterations;
  • Track new AI models and tools; be the company's go-to expert on what's creatively possible with AI, staying hands-on in the tools;
  • Run regular R&D and build prompt and style libraries that keep quality consistent as the team grows;
  • Stay hands-on: jump into the tools (Figma, Adobe Suite, AI platforms) when needed to unblock the team, take on the most complex creatives, or test new approaches;
  • Partner with the Generative AI Pipeline Engineer to turn the team's creative needs into pipelines, presets, and automation;
  • Work tightly with Creative Producers, Marketers, Media Buyers, and Video Editors: align on strategy, negotiate deadlines, solve bottlenecks.

Requirements

Your must-haves

You don't need to meet every single requirement. If you're excellent in most of these areas and can show shipped work, we'd love to hear from you.

  • 5+ years of Leadership Experience: You have successfully managed creative/design teams in digital marketing. (This is not a role for a senior designer looking for their first management gig);

  • Strong Project Manager: You drive every project cleanly to the finish line. You guarantee top-tier quality, maintain absolute order, and hit strict deadlines without excuses;
  • Strong Visual Craft: composition, lighting, color, typography, anatomy. You can articulate exactly why a creative works or doesn't;
  • Design Toolstack: proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite; comfortable connecting AI outputs with traditional design pipelines;
  • AI Geek: far beyond basic prompting. You track every new model release and can't wait to test how it could level up ad creatives. Hands-on with modern AI image platforms (Figma Weave, Higgsfield, Magnific, Runway, or similar), using them for creating photorealistic visuals. Able to choose the right tool for each task, as well as to catch and fix artifacts.
  • Performance Marketing DNA: solid understanding of static ad creatives (Google, Meta, and other paid channels). You know what stops the scroll, what makes a visual sell, and how creative decisions move CTR, CPA, and conversion rate;

Nice to have

jobs.excerpt: About Practifi (The Real Story)Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey.
jobs.description:
About Practifi (The Real Story)

Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.

That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.

The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)

When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.

Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.

We're creating this role to change that. As our Data QA Analyst, you'll be the dedicated owner of data migration quality across every client onboarding engagement. You'll work the checklist object by object, build one standard the whole team uses, and spot the patterns a single-project view misses. You'll be a big part of why a client's first login feels like their business, not a spreadsheet import.

Your Day-to-Day (The Honest Version)

The Core Work

  • Validate every migration end to end. You'll analyze source data (record counts, missing values, duplicates, orphaned contacts, inconsistent values), then walk through the Practifi interface object by object to confirm everything displays and connects the way the client's Data Mapping Document says it should.
  • Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
  • Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
  • Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
  • Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
  • Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.

The Reality Check

The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.

You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.

The Growth

This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.

You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. We promote from within. A role that sees every engagement is a strong foundation for a path into consulting, data engineering, or delivery leadership.

What We're Really Looking For

The Must-Haves

  • 3 to 5 years of experience in data quality, data migration, data validation, or quality assurance, ideally in a CRM or software environment
  • Hands-on experience reconciling data: comparing record counts, running field-by-field checks, and finding duplicate and orphaned records
  • Comfort working inside Salesforce or a comparable CRM, navigating objects, records, and related lists
  • A working understanding of how relational data fits together (IDs, lookups, and records that link other records)
  • Experience logging and tracking issues in JIRA, Asana, or a similar tool
  • Clear written communication, including findings a non-technical stakeholder can act on

The Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with Salesforce Inspector, the Salesforce Developer Console, Data Loader, or SOQL queries
  • Background in wealth management, financial services, or another regulated industry
  • Experience supporting client onboarding or software implementation projects
  • Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivot tables, conditional formatting)

A Salesforce certification isn't required to apply. You'll earn one with us.

The More Important Stuff

  • You’re observant and tuned into the details within the data.
  • You care about the cause of an issue, not just the fix.
  • You're comfortable telling a Project Manager something they don't want to hear, and you do it early and kindly.
  • You like building structure where there isn't any yet.
  • You're honest about what you don't know and curious enough to go find out.

What Taking This Leap Gets You

The Practical Stuff

  • Base salary: $78,000 to $95,000. We share the range because you deserve to know it before you apply. Where you land depends on your experience against the role.
  • Generous time off: 20 days of paid vacation, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 3 volunteering days annually
  • Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance benefits, plus a 401(k) with company match

•Fully remote within the US

The Cultural Stuff

  • A Practibuddy mentor from your first day, so you always have someone to ask
  • An annual Learnbucks education stipend for the courses and certifications you choose
  • Bi-annual in-person summits in Chicago where the whole company gets together
  • A Slack culture where questions are welcome and wins get celebrated
  • Remote-first that's real: genuine work-life integration, not a line in a job ad

Living Our Values Daily

  • Growth: You'll be part of building a function from the ground up, with Learnbucks and a real promotion path behind you.
  • Collaboration: You'll partner with every delivery role on every engagement, and the fix is always a team effort.
  • Transparency: The salary is in this ad, and your QA findings will be shared openly, good news and bad.
  • Curiosity: When you see patterns in the data, you'll be the one asking why.
  • Integrity: You'll sign off when the data is right, not when the calendar says it should be.

Ready to Join Our Community?

This role sits in our Data Services team within the Enablement organization and reports to our Project Management Office (PMO) Team Lead. You'll work closely with Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers across every engagement. The role is fully remote within the US and does not provide Visa sponsorship (must be legally authorized to work in the US for any employer without sponsorship).

One Last Thing:

We're not just hiring a Data QA Analyst. We're adding someone to our community who'll make sure every client's first impression of Practifi is one we're proud of. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Practifi is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We value transparency in our hiring process. All final hiring decisions are made by our human recruitment team, ensuring fair and thoughtful consideration for every applicant.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewAt iGrafx, we help organizations turn process into competitive advantage.
jobs.description:
Overview

At iGrafx, we help organizations turn process into competitive advantage. By combining process intelligence, AI, and automation, we enable enterprises to understand how work gets done, identify where it can be improved, and confidently transform the processes that matter most.

Every business process now has three participants: people, automation, and AI agents. Enterprises are deploying agents faster than they can govern them — and in regulated industries, an agent without process context is an operational risk, not an efficiency gain. The iGrafx Agentic Process Foundation is the process intelligence layer that gives AI agents the visibility, context, and guardrails they need to operate reliably. It is the most urgent conversation in our market, and this role exists to go have it.

We are looking for a Senior Account Executive to own full-cycle enterprise sales for the Agentic Process Foundation across North America. This is a quota-carrying, build-it-yourself seat. You will source the majority of your own pipeline, run your own outreach, earn your own executive meetings, and close six-figure deals with operations, transformation, risk, and technology leaders who are under pressure to make AI work safely at scale.

This is deliberately not a coverage role on a mature patch. There is no inbound firehose, no dedicated BDR pod feeding you meetings, and no brand that opens doors on its own in every account you will call into. What there is: a differentiated product in a category buyers are actively budgeting for, three decades of process credibility behind it, direct access to leadership, and the freedom to run your territory like it is your own business.

We hire for hunger, commercial judgment, and the determination to deliver results. Our strongest sellers are ambitious without ego, comfortable operating with autonomy and ambiguity, and committed to winning as a team. If you have carried a number somewhere you had to create demand rather than harvest it, this is a role where that muscle is the whole job.

Our Core Values

At iGrafx, we believe in empowering our people to make an impact. We value integrity, teamwork, accountability, and customer success above all. Our mission extends beyond revenue; we help clients achieve operational excellence, manage risk, and accelerate transformation through the power of process intelligence. Check out our core values, and if they resonate with you, consider joining our team.

The role

We are looking for an Account Executive to grow our business across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. You will win new mid-market and enterprise customers and expand our relationships with existing DACH accounts. You will own the full sales cycle, from first conversation to signed contract, and work closely with our presales, customer success and partner teams.

What you will do

  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline of new-logo opportunities in mid-market and enterprise accounts across DACH
  • Grow existing customers through upsell and cross-sell of the iGrafx platform, including our new AI framework – Agentic Process Foundation
  • Run complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles with leaders in operations, transformation, quality, IT and finance
  • Lead discovery, build business cases and present value to C-level and senior decision makers
  • Work with presales on demos, proofs of value and solution design
  • Develop joint opportunities with consulting and technology partners in the region
  • Forecast accurately and keep opportunity data current in Salesforce using a structured qualification method (e.g. MEDDPICC)
  • Represent iGrafx at customer events, trade fairs and industry meetups across EMEA
  • Meet and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets

What you bring

  • 5+ years of B2B software sales experience in AI, process intelligence, BPM or Operational Excellence (Lean, Six Sigma, continuous improvement)
  • A proven record of meeting or exceeding quota in mid-market and enterprise accounts
  • Experience with both new-logo acquisition and growing existing accounts
  • Confidence selling complex solutions to senior business and IT stakeholders
  • An established network in the DACH market
  • Native-level German and fluent business English
  • Self-driven and organised, comfortable working remotely in an international team
  • Willingness to travel within EMEA (around 20%)

Nice to have

  • SaaS sales experience with consumption or subscription models
  • Familiarity with structured sales methods such as MEDDPICC, Challenger or Value Selling
  • Experience working with consulting and system-integrator partners
  • Knowledge of regulated industries such as manufacturing, automotive, financial services or pharma

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary plus an attractive, uncapped commission plan
  • A fully remote role
  • A modern platform at the intersection of AI and process intelligence
  • A strong, established customer base in DACH to build on
  • An international, collaborative team with short decision paths

Reporting Structure

Reports to: VP, Sales EMEA

iGrafx Company Description

iGrafx is a global leader in process intelligence, helping organizations understand, improve, and transform the processes that power their business. By bringing together process intelligence, process mining, modeling, simulation, and AI, iGrafx gives enterprises the visibility and context they need to make smarter decisions, accelerate transformation, and achieve measurable business outcomes.

For more than three decades, iGrafx has helped shape the business process management industry. From pioneering process diagramming and simulation technologies to contributing to the development of BPMN and advancing enterprise process modeling, innovation in process has been at the core of who we are.

Today, that foundation is increasingly important as enterprises embrace AI. AI is only as effective as the processes and business context behind it. iGrafx helps organizations build that foundation — connecting people, processes, systems, and data so they can identify opportunities for improvement, understand the impact of change, and deploy AI and automation with greater confidence and control.

Trusted by organizations around the world, iGrafx supports global enterprises across highly complex and regulated industries. With an international presence and a partner ecosystem spanning more than 20 countries, we combine global scale with deep process expertise.

Our mission remains focused: to turn process into competitive advantage. For our customers, that means more efficient operations, better decisions, reduced risk, and measurable ROI. For our employees, it means the opportunity to help define the next generation of process intelligence and play a meaningful role in how enterprises transform in the age of AI.

iGrafx is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome everyone to our team. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
